gancho: Na Segunda Guerra, o alemão Walter Baade, tido como "inimigo estrangeiro" nos EUA, ganhou céus mais escuros com o blecaute de Los Angeles. Viu estrelas no centro de Andrômeda e acabou dobrando o tamanho do universo.
explicacao: Baade, nascido na Alemanha, trabalhava no Observatório do Monte Wilson, perto de Los Angeles, desde 1931. Quando os Estados Unidos entraram na guerra, foi classificado como "inimigo estrangeiro". Segundo um relato, isso veio com um toque de recolher que o impediria de observar à noite, até que um colega conseguiu uma exceção para ele. A situação acabou jogando a favor: com muitos astrônomos ocupados em trabalhos de guerra e as luzes da cidade reduzidas para proteger a navegação na costa, ele teve mais acesso aos telescópios e céus mais escuros. Assim fotografou estrelas nas regiões internas de Andrômeda, que até então ninguém tinha conseguido distinguir, num feito que se julgava impossível com o telescópio de 100 polegadas. As estrelas mais brilhantes do núcleo eram vermelhas, e não azuis como nos braços espirais, e Baade concluiu que havia duas populações de estrelas. Essas observações também o levaram a descobrir que existem dois tipos de cefeidas, as estrelas usadas para medir distâncias. Anos depois, já com o novo telescópio de 200 polegadas, ele procurou em Andrômeda estrelas variáveis que deveriam aparecer se ela estivesse à distância aceita, de 750 mil anos-luz, e não as encontrou. Concluiu que a galáxia estava mais longe e anunciou isso em 1952, na reunião da União Astronômica Internacional em Roma: na prática, o tamanho do universo conhecido dobrava.

fontes.titulo: Baade, Wilhelm Heinrich Walter (Complete Dictionary of Scientific Biography, via Encyclopedia.com)
fontes.trecho: When the United States entered World War II, Baade was classified as an enemy alien, but this favored rather than hampered his astronomical career: with many astronomers engaged in war work, and the lights of Los Angeles dimmed to protect coastal shipping, Baade had increased access to the telescopes and the added advantage of darker skies. Under these favorable circumstances he was able to photograph stars in the hitherto unresolved inner portions of the Andromeda galaxy, M31, and in both of its satellite galaxies, M32 and NGC205 (1944). This achievement was both technically difficult—thought, indeed to be unattainable with the 100-inch telescope he used—and theoretically significant, because the brightest stars in the nucleus of M31 turned out to be red—not blue, as in the surrounding spiral arms. Baade realized he was dealing with two different stellar populations [...] Baade reasoned correctly that the galaxy was more distant than had previously been thought. Announced in 1952 at the Rome meeting of the International Astronomical Union, this conclusion cleared up several inconsistencies, but also essentially doubled the size of the universe. [...] when he looked for cluster-type variables in the Andromeda galaxy. At the accepted distance of 750,000 light-years, these stars should have appeared in photographs taken with the 200-inch telescope; when they did not

fontes.titulo: March 24, 1893: The birth of Walter Baade (Astronomy)
fontes.trecho: Baade joined the staff of the Mount Wilson Observatory in 1931. His German background earned him "enemy alien" status during World War II – and a curfew that would keep Baade from nighttime observations. But when a colleague was able to wrangle an exemption for him, the wartime blackout made for extraordinarily dark skies and groundbreaking discoveries.

was a German astronomer who worked in the United States from 1931 to 1959. [...] During World War II, while working at Mount Wilson Observatory, Baade took advantage of wartime blackout conditions (which reduced light pollution), to resolve stars in the center of the Andromeda Galaxy for the first time. These observations led him to define distinct "populations" for stars (Population I and Population II). The same observations led him to discover that there are two types of Cepheid variable stars.

gancho: A famosa colisão entre a Via Láctea e Andrômeda virou dúvida: um estudo de 2025 deu quase 50% de chance de não haver fusão em 10 bilhões de anos; outro, de 2026, voltou a cerca de 90% de chance de fusão.
explicacao: Andrômeda vem na nossa direção a cerca de 110 km/s, o que se sabe pelo desvio para o azul da sua luz. O difícil é medir o movimento lateral dela no céu, e é dele que depende se haverá um choque ou só uma passagem ao largo. A equipe de Till Sawala usou dados dos telescópios espaciais Gaia e Hubble e rodou 100 mil simulações. A M33, do Triângulo, aumentava a chance de fusão, enquanto a Grande Nuvem de Magalhães, cuja órbita é perpendicular à rota entre a Via Láctea e Andrômeda, a reduzia. Com as incertezas de posições, movimentos e massas, cerca de metade dos cenários não terminava em fusão nos próximos 10 bilhões de anos. Para os autores, o destino da nossa galáxia "ainda está completamente em aberto". Depois, uma equipe da Universidade de Pequim liderada pelo doutorando Hao Wu e pelo professor Huawei Zhang mediu de novo o movimento lateral de Andrômeda com estrelas supergigantes e resolveu discrepâncias entre as medições do Gaia. O resultado, publicado em 2026: cerca de 90% de chance de fusão em 10 bilhões de anos, com tempo médio de uns 6,5 bilhões. Mesmo assim, esses autores dizem que a questão continua inconclusiva, porque pequenas mudanças no movimento medido alteram bastante o desfecho. E, se a fusão acontecer, é improvável que duas estrelas colidam: a distância entre elas é imensa.

fontes.titulo: No certainty of a Milky Way–Andromeda collision (Nature Astronomy, 2025)
fontes.trecho: Published: 02 June 2025 [...] It is commonly believed that our own Milky Way is on a collision course with the neighbouring Andromeda galaxy. As a result of their merger, predicted in around 5 billion years, the two large spiral galaxies that define the present Local Group would form a new elliptical galaxy. Here we consider the latest and most accurate observations by the Gaia and Hubble space telescopes, along with recent consensus mass estimates, to derive possible future scenarios and identify the main sources of uncertainty in the evolution of the Local Group over the next 10 billion years. We found that the next most massive Local Group member galaxies—namely, M33 and the Large Magellanic Cloud—distinctly and radically affect the Milky Way–Andromeda orbit. Although including M33 increases the merger probability, the orbit of the Large Magellanic Cloud runs perpendicular to the Milky Way–Andromeda orbit and makes their merger less probable. In the full system, we found that uncertainties in the present positions, motions and masses of all galaxies leave room for drastically different outcomes and a probability of close to 50% that there will be no Milky Way–Andromeda merger during the next 10 billion years. Based on the best available data, the fate of our Galaxy is still completely open.

The stars involved are sufficiently spaced that it is improbable that any of them would individually collide, though some stars may be ejected. [...] The Andromeda Galaxy is approaching the Milky Way at about 110 kilometres per second (68.4 mi/s) as indicated by blueshift. However, the lateral speed (measured as proper motion) is very difficult to measure with sufficient precision to draw reasonable conclusions. By 2012, it appeared to be that a collision with the two galaxies was highly likely. [...] In 2025, Till Sawala and colleagues found that, with data gathered from the Gaia spacecraft and Hubble telescope which was not available in 2012, the chance for a collision is much lower. Astronomers considered 22 different variables which could affect the potential collision between the Milky Way and Andromeda galaxies and ran 100,000 simulations based on these variables known as Monte Carlo Simulations. [...] there is only a 2% chance of a head-on collision in the next 4 to 5 billion years. [...] the chance of even two stars colliding is negligible because of the huge distances between the stars.

fontes.titulo: The Fate of the Milky Way–Andromeda System: To Merge or Not? (KIAA, Universidade de Pequim)
fontes.trecho: Using improved dynamical measurements, PhD student Hao Wu and Professor Huawei Zhang in the Department of Astronomy at Peking University led a team of astronomers to determine that the probability of a merger between the Milky Way and Andromeda is 90% within the next 10 billion years. [...] Although previous evidence was contradictory, the team resolved these discrepancies using improved stellar samples, showing that a merger is likely in about 6.5 billion years. [...] Using the Gaia results, Sawala et al. (2025) in Nature Astronomy suggested that the probability of a Milky Way–M31 merger within the next 10 billion years might be only about 50%. [...] Wu, Zhang, and their collaborators constructed high-quality samples of supergiant stars in Andromeda and the nearby Triangulum Galaxy (M33) [...] the probability of a MW–M31 merger within the next 10 Gyr is approximately 90% (see Figure 4), with a median merger time of about 6.5 Gyr. [...] More importantly, the study shows that even small changes in M31's proper motion can significantly alter the future orbital evolution of the Milky Way–M31 system. [...] although the current results support the picture in which the Milky Way and M31 will ultimately merge, the question remains inconclusive. [...] The Astrophysical Journal Letters (Wu et al. 2026, ApJL, 1001, L19)

gancho: Os braços de uma galáxia espiral não seriam feitos sempre das mesmas estrelas. Pela teoria das ondas de densidade, eles funcionam como um engarrafamento: as estrelas entram, se apertam um tempo e saem.
explicacao: Se os braços fossem estruturas fixas de matéria, haveria um problema. As estrelas perto do centro giram mais depressa que as da borda, e os braços se enrolariam cada vez mais, até sumirem no resto da galáxia depois de poucas voltas. É o chamado problema do enrolamento. Em 1964, C. C. Lin e Frank Shu propuseram que os braços são regiões de maior densidade que giram num ritmo próprio, diferente do das estrelas. A comparação é com um congestionamento numa estrada: os carros atravessam o trecho lento, que se move mais devagar do que eles. Na galáxia, estrelas, gás e poeira passam pelas ondas, são comprimidos e seguem em frente, e a própria atração gravitacional entre as estrelas mantém o desenho espiral. A teoria ajuda a explicar por que os braços concentram estrelas jovens: quando nuvens de gás são comprimidas, algumas colapsam e formam estrelas. As mais quentes e maciças vivem pouco e morrem antes de sair da onda, enquanto as menores e mais vermelhas escapam e se espalham pelo disco. A mesma física foi aplicada depois aos anéis de Saturno, que têm ondas espirais criadas pelas luas do planeta.

fontes.trecho: Density wave theory or the Lin–Shu density wave theory is a theory proposed by C.C. Lin and Frank Shu in the mid-1960s to explain the spiral arm structure of spiral galaxies. [...] In this hypothesis, the spiral pattern rotates with a particular angular frequency (pattern speed), whereas the stars in the galactic disk orbit at varying speeds, which depend on their distance to the galaxy center. [...] Originally, astronomers had the idea that the arms of a spiral galaxy were material. However, if this were the case, then the arms would become more and more tightly wound, since the matter nearer to the center of the galaxy rotates faster than the matter at the edge of the galaxy. The arms would become indistinguishable from the rest of the galaxy after only a few orbits. This is called the winding problem. Lin & Shu proposed in 1964 that the arms were not material in nature, but instead made up of areas of greater density, similar to a traffic jam on a highway. The cars move through the traffic jam: the density of cars increases in the middle of it. The traffic jam itself, however, moves more slowly. In the galaxy, stars, gas, dust, and other components move through the density waves, are compressed, and then move out of them. More specifically, the density wave theory argues that the "gravitational attraction between stars at different radii" prevents the so-called winding problem, and actually maintains the spiral pattern. [...] When clouds of gas and dust enter into a density wave and are compressed, the rate of star formation increases as some clouds meet the Jeans criterion, and collapse to form new stars. [...] The hot OB stars that are created ionize the gas of the interstellar medium, and form H II regions. These stars have relatively short lifetimes, however, and expire before fully leaving the density wave. The smaller, redder stars do leave the wave, and become distributed throughout the galactic disk. [...] Peter Goldreich, Frank Shu, and others applied density wave theory to the rings of Saturn. Saturn's rings (particularly the A Ring) contain a great many spiral density waves and spiral bending waves excited by Lindblad resonances and vertical resonances (respectively) with Saturn's moons.
The spiral arms are thought to be areas of high-density matter, or "density waves".

gancho: Em 2007, uma professora holandesa que classificava galáxias como voluntária achou uma mancha estranha no céu, ao lado de uma galáxia. Parece ser um "eco": gás iluminado por um quasar que talvez já tenha se apagado.
explicacao: Hanny van Arkel participava do Galaxy Zoo, projeto de ciência cidadã em que voluntários pela internet ajudam a classificar imagens de galáxias. A mancha, batizada de Hanny's Voorwerp ("o objeto de Hanny", em holandês), fica ao lado da galáxia espiral IC 2497, a cerca de 650 milhões de anos-luz, e tem o tamanho de uma pequena galáxia. O verde das imagens do Hubble é uma cor convencional, usada para mostrar o brilho do oxigênio. Uma hipótese é que a nuvem seja o resto de uma pequena galáxia, iluminado pela radiação de um quasar que brilhou no centro de IC 2497 cerca de 100 mil anos antes do momento em que a vemos. O quasar não aparece nas imagens e pode ter se desligado nos últimos 200 mil anos. Como a luz leva dezenas de milhares de anos para ir da galáxia até a nuvem, a nuvem ainda mostraria um "eco" de um passado que a galáxia já não exibe. Outra proposta, de 2010, é que parte da luz venha também da interação de um jato de partículas do buraco negro central com o gás em volta da galáxia. Depois, voluntários do mesmo projeto fizeram uma busca ampla e encontraram 19 galáxias com nuvens parecidas, apelidadas de Voorwerpjes, "objetinhos".

fontes.trecho: Hanny's Voorwerp (Dutch for Hanny's object) is an instance of an astronomical phenomenon called a quasar ionization echo. It was discovered in 2007 by Dutch schoolteacher Hanny van Arkel while she was participating as a volunteer in the Galaxy Zoo project, part of the Zooniverse group of citizen science websites. Photographically, it appears as a bright blob close to spiral galaxy IC 2497 in the constellation Leo Minor. [...] Hanny's Voorwerp (HsV) is about the size of a small galaxy and has a central hole over 16,000 light years across. In an image taken with the Hubble Space Telescope, HsV is colored green, a standard false color that is used to represent the presence of several luminous emission lines of glowing oxygen. HsV has been shown to be at the same distance from Earth as the adjacent galaxy IC 2497, which is about 650 million light-years away. [...] One hypothesis suggests that HsV consists of remnants of a small galaxy showing the impact of radiation from a bright quasar event that occurred in the center of IC 2497 about 100,000 years before how it is observed today. The quasar event is thought to have stimulated the bright emission that characterizes HsV. The quasar might have switched off in the last 200,000 years and is not visible in the available images. [...] In this case, its effects on HsV would be still visible because of the distance of several tens of thousands of light years between HsV and the quasar in the nearby galaxy: HsV would show a "light echo" or "ghost image" of events that are older than those currently seen in the galaxy. [...] They hypothesized that the light comes from two sources: (1) a supermassive black hole at the center of IC 2497, and (2) light produced by an interaction of an energetic jet from the black hole and the gas surrounding IC 2497. [...] participants in the Galaxy Zoo (GZ) project carried out a wide search for such clouds using data from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS). This search yielded a list of 19 galaxies with AGN-photoionized clouds detected to beyond 10 kiloparsecs from the nuclei. These were nicknamed 'Voorwerpjes' from the Dutch for 'small objects'. [...] On 17 June 2010, a group of researchers at the European VLBI Network (EVN) and the UK's Multi-Element Radio Linked Interferometer Network (MERLIN), proposed another related explanation.

gancho: Há uns 8 a 10 bilhões de anos, a Via Láctea teria engolido uma galáxia anã num choque frontal. Os restos dela ainda estão aqui: estrelas em órbitas esticadas "como agulhas", achadas com o satélite Gaia.
explicacao: A galáxia destruída ganhou dois apelidos. "Salsicha de Gaia" vem da forma de salsicha que as estrelas dela desenham num gráfico de velocidades feito com dados do satélite europeu Gaia. Já Gaia-Enceladus lembra o gigante da mitologia grega enterrado sob o monte Etna, que causava terremotos: a galáxia também foi "enterrada" na Via Láctea e a sacudiu. Segundo os astrônomos, ela chegou numa órbita muito excêntrica e se despedaçou rapidamente, e por isso suas estrelas passam muito perto do centro da galáxia. Somando gás, estrelas e matéria escura, ela tinha mais de 10 bilhões de vezes a massa do Sol, e trouxe pelo menos oito aglomerados globulares, bolas densas de estrelas que galáxias pequenas não costumam ter. O impacto provavelmente inchou ou até rompeu o disco da Via Láctea, que teve de formar um disco novo. Os destroços se espalharam pelas partes internas e ajudaram a formar o bojo central e o halo de estrelas que envolve a galáxia. Foi a última grande fusão da Via Láctea. Fusões menores continuam: a galáxia anã de Sagitário está sendo absorvida agora mesmo.

fontes.titulo: The Gaia Sausage: the major collision that changed the Milky Way (University of Cambridge)
fontes.trecho: The astronomers propose that around eight to 10 billion years ago, an unknown dwarf galaxy smashed into our own Milky Way. The dwarf did not survive the impact. It quickly fell apart, and the wreckage is now all around us. "The collision ripped the dwarf to shreds, leaving its stars moving on very radial orbits, like needles," said Vasily Belokurov [...] "These stars' paths take them very close to the centre of our galaxy. This is a tell-tale sign that the dwarf galaxy came in on a really eccentric orbit and its fate was sealed." [...] These Sausage stars are what's left of the last major merger of the Milky Way." There are ongoing mergers taking place right now, such as between the puny Sagittarius dwarf galaxy and the Milky Way. However, the Sausage galaxy was much more massive. Its total mass in gas, stars and dark matter was more than 10 billion times the mass of our sun. [...] The Sausage's piercing trajectory meant that the Milky Way's disk was probably puffed up or even fractured following the impact, and the Milky Way had to re-grow a new disk. At the same time, the Sausage debris was scattered all around the inner parts of the Milky Way, creating the 'bulge' at the galaxy's centre and the surrounding 'stellar halo'. [...] The new research also identified at least eight large, spherical clumps of stars called globular clusters that were brought into the Milky Way by the Sausage galaxy. Small galaxies do not normally have globular clusters of their own

The "Gaia Sausage" is so-called because of the characteristic sausage shape of the population in a chart of velocity space [...] using data from the Gaia Mission. [...] The name "Enceladus" refers to the mythological giant Enceladus, who was buried under Mount Etna and caused earthquakes. Similarly, this former galaxy was buried in the Milky Way, and caused the puffing up of the thick disc.

gancho: A galáxia anã de Sagitário já atravessou o disco da Via Láctea pelo menos três vezes. Um estudo sugere que as passagens dispararam surtos de nascimento de estrelas, e o Sol pode ter surgido num deles.
explicacao: Sagitário é uma pequena galáxia satélite, cerca de 10 mil vezes menos massiva que a nossa, descoberta só em 1994, embora seja uma das vizinhas mais próximas. Ela fica do outro lado do centro galáctico em relação à Terra, e por isso parece muito fraca. Sua órbita vai se apertando, e a cada travessia do disco ela perde parte do gás e da poeira. Pelos modelos, as passagens ocorreram há cerca de 5 ou 6 bilhões, 2 bilhões e 1 bilhão de anos. Uma equipe liderada por Tomás Ruiz-Lara, do Instituto de Astrofísica de Canárias, analisou dados do satélite Gaia sobre estrelas num raio de uns 6.500 anos-luz em volta do Sol e achou três picos de formação de estrelas, há 5,7, 1,9 e 1 bilhão de anos, coincidindo com as passagens. A ideia é que cada choque agite o gás da Via Láctea como ondas na água, concentrando material em algumas regiões até que ele forme estrelas. Um dos surtos coincide, grosso modo, com a formação do Sol, há uns 4,7 bilhões de anos. Os autores ressalvam que não sabem se a nuvem que deu origem ao Sol colapsou por causa de Sagitário, mas dizem que é um cenário possível.

fontes.titulo: Galactic crash may have triggered Solar System formation (ESA)
fontes.trecho: Astronomers have known that Sagittarius repeatedly smashes through the Milky Way's disc, as its orbit around the galaxy's core tightens as a result of gravitational forces. [...] Some even claim that the 10 000 times more massive Milky Way's trademark spiral structure might be a result of the at least three known crashes with Sagittarius over the past six billion years. [...] The ripples caused by the collisions seem to have triggered major star formation episodes, one of which roughly coincided with the time of the formation of the Sun some 4.7 billion years ago. "It is known from existing models that Sagittarius fell into the Milky Way three times – first about five or six billion years ago, then about two billion years ago, and finally one billion years ago," says Tomás Ruiz-Lara, a researcher in Astrophysics at the Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias (IAC) in Tenerife, Spain, and lead author of the new study published in Nature Astronomy. "When we looked into the Gaia data about the Milky Way, we found three periods of increased star formation that peaked 5.7 billion years ago, 1.9 billion years ago and 1 billion years ago, corresponding with the time when Sagittarius is believed to have passed through the disc of the Milky Way." [...] The researchers looked at luminosities, distances and colours of stars within a sphere of about 6500 light years around the Sun [...] causing all the previously still gas and dust inside the larger galaxy to slosh around like ripples on the water." In some areas of the Milky Way, these ripples would lead to higher concentrations of dust and gas, while emptying others. The high density of material in those areas would then trigger the formation of new stars. [...] "We don't know if the particular cloud of gas and dust that turned into the Sun collapsed because of the effects of Sagittarius or not. But it is a possible scenario because the age of the Sun is consistent with a star formed as a result of the Sagittarius effect." Every collision stripped Sagittarius of some of its gas and dust, leaving the galaxy smaller after each passage.

Officially discovered in 1994, by Rodrigo Ibata, Mike Irwin, and Gerry Gilmore, Sgr dSph was immediately recognized as being the nearest known neighbor to the Milky Way at the time. [...] Although it is one of the closest companion galaxies to the Milky Way, the main parent cluster is on the opposite side of the Galactic Center from Earth, and consequently is very faint, although covering a large area of the sky.

gancho: Uma estrela a uns 29 mil anos-luz da Terra corre a 1.755 km/s e está sendo expulsa da Via Láctea. Refazendo a rota dela, astrônomos viram que foi arremessada pelo buraco negro do centro da galáxia.
explicacao: A estrela, chamada S5-HVS1, foi achada por acaso num levantamento de velocidades de estrelas do céu do sul, o S5, e a descoberta é creditada a Sergey Koposov, da Universidade Carnegie Mellon. Ela tem cerca de 2,35 vezes a massa do Sol e fica na constelação do Grou. Sua velocidade é de quase 0,6% da velocidade da luz. Quando os pesquisadores calcularam a órbita de trás para a frente, ela apontou sem ambiguidade para o centro galáctico: a estrela teria sido lançada de perto de Sagitário A*, o buraco negro supermassivo de lá, a cerca de 1.800 km/s, e viajado 4,8 milhões de anos até onde está hoje. A explicação proposta é o mecanismo de Hills: a estrela fazia parte de um par, e a gravidade do buraco negro desfez o sistema e a atirou para longe. Se foi isso, é o primeiro exemplo conhecido desse mecanismo. Em novembro de 2019, ela era a estrela de sequência principal (a fase de vida em que está o Sol) mais rápida já detectada, e sua velocidade de lançamento é quase o dobro da de outras estrelas hipervelozes ligadas ao centro da galáxia, o que levanta dúvidas sobre se todas foram lançadas do mesmo jeito.

fontes.titulo: The Great Escape: Discovery of a nearby 1700 km/s star ejected from the Milky Way by Sgr A* (Koposov et al., MNRAS)
fontes.trecho: We present the serendipitous discovery of the fastest Main Sequence hyper-velocity star (HVS) by the Southern Stellar Stream Spectroscopic Survey (S5). The star S5-HVS1 is a $\sim 2.35$ M$_\odot$ A-type star [...] The current 3-D velocity of the star in the Galactic frame is $1755\pm50$ km/s. When integrated backwards in time, the orbit of the star points unambiguously to the Galactic Centre, implying that S5-HVS1 was kicked away from Sgr A* with a velocity of $\sim 1800$ km/s and travelled for $4.8$ Myr to its current location. [...] With the S5-HVS1 ejection velocity being almost twice the velocity of other hyper-velocity stars previously associated with the Galactic Centre, we question whether they have been generated by the same mechanism

S5-HVS1 is an A-type main-sequence star notable as the fastest one detected as of November 2019, and has been determined to be traveling with a peculiar velocity of 1,755 km/s (3,930,000 mph), almost 0.6% of the speed of light. The star is in the southern constellation Grus, and about 29,000 light-years from Earth. According to astronomers, S5-HVS1 was ejected from the Milky Way galaxy after interacting with Sagittarius A*, the supermassive black hole at the center of the galaxy. It is possible that it was originally part of a binary system that was tidally disrupted by the supermassive black hole, causing it to be ejected. If this is the case, that it was flung out of the galaxy by the central black hole, it is then the first known example of a star that has undergone the Hills mechanism. The star's discovery has been credited to Sergey Koposov, assistant professor of physics at Carnegie Mellon University, as part of the Southern Stellar Stream Spectroscopic Survey (S5). [...] S5-HVS1 is an A-type main-sequence star notable as the fastest one detected as of November 2019

gancho: Em 1995, o diretor do instituto do Hubble apontou o telescópio por 10 dias para um pedaço "vazio" do céu. Colegas acharam desperdício. A imagem revelou cerca de 3 mil galáxias, algumas entre as mais distantes já vistas.
explicacao: O pedaço escolhido, na Ursa Maior, tem 1/24.000.000 da área do céu: é como uma bola de tênis vista a 100 metros. Robert Williams, então diretor do Instituto de Ciência do Telescópio Espacial, tinha à sua disposição uma parte do tempo do Hubble. Segundo ele, o comitê que distribui o tempo do telescópio nunca aprovaria um projeto tão longo e arriscado. Os colegas diziam que era uma péssima ideia, que as galáxias distantes seriam fracas demais para aparecer e que mais um fracasso seria um desastre de imagem para um telescópio que tinha acabado de ter a visão consertada por astronautas. Williams disse que, se fosse tão ruim assim, pediria demissão. Entre 18 e 28 de dezembro de 1995, o Hubble fez 342 exposições da região. Quase todos os cerca de 3 mil objetos da imagem são galáxias, muitas jovens, algumas a cerca de 12 bilhões de anos-luz. Elas eram bem mais irregulares e perturbadas que as de hoje, porque colisões eram mais comuns no universo jovem. Um dos céticos, o astrônomo Robert Kirshner, admitiu depois: "Bob estava certo, eu estava errado".

fontes.trecho: The Hubble Deep Field (HDF) is an image of a small region in the constellation Ursa Major, constructed from a series of observations by the Hubble Space Telescope. It covers an area about 2.6 arcminutes on a side, about one 24-millionth of the whole sky, which is equivalent in angular size to a tennis ball at a distance of 100 metres. The image was assembled from 342 separate exposures taken with the Space Telescope's Wide Field and Planetary Camera 2 over ten consecutive days between December 18 and 28, 1995. The field is so small that only a few foreground stars in the Milky Way lie within it; thus, almost all of the 3,000 objects in the image are galaxies, some of which are among the youngest and most distant known. [...] The HDF, however, contained many galaxies with redshifts as high as six, corresponding to distances of about 12 billion light-years. [...] The HDF galaxies contained a considerably larger proportion of disturbed and irregular galaxies than the local universe; galaxy collisions and mergers were more common in the young universe as it was much smaller than today.

fontes.titulo: When Hubble Stared at Nothing for 100 Hours (National Geographic)
fontes.trecho: It was a terrible idea, his colleagues told him, and a waste of valuable telescope time. [...] no way would the distant galaxies Williams hoped to see be bright enough for Hubble to detect. Plus, another Hubble failure would be a public relations nightmare. [...] Not much earlier, astronauts had dragged Hubble into the cargo bay of the space shuttle Endeavour and corrected a disastrous flaw in the prized telescope's vision. [...] As director of the Space Telescope Science Institute, he had a certain amount of Hubble's time at his personal disposal. "The telescope allocation committee would never have approved such a long, risky project," he explains. [...] "If it's that bad, I'll resign. [...] He was among the scientists who initially thought the deep field was a bad idea. "Bob was right, I was wrong.

gancho: A Via Láctea e as galáxias vizinhas são puxadas rumo a uma concentração de matéria chamada Grande Atrator. Ela fica justo atrás do disco da nossa galáxia, onde poeira e estrelas atrapalham a visão.
explicacao: Além de se afastarem com a expansão do universo, as galáxias têm movimentos próprios, causados pela gravidade de regiões com mais ou menos matéria. Nos anos 1980, sete astrônomos apelidados de "Sete Samurais" estudaram cerca de 400 galáxias elípticas, compararam as distâncias com as velocidades e acharam um fluxo coerente de galáxias rumo a uma concentração até então desconhecida, a uns 150 a 250 milhões de anos-luz, na direção do aglomerado de Norma. O problema é que ela fica na Zona de Evitação, a faixa do céu escondida pelo plano da Via Láctea, e por isso é estudada com raios X, rádio e infravermelho, que atravessam melhor a poeira. Em 2014, astrônomos definiram nosso "bairro" cósmico pelos fluxos das galáxias, como uma bacia de atração com o Grande Atrator no centro: Laniakea, cerca de 100 mil galáxias. O nome, sugerido por um professor de língua havaiana, quer dizer "céu imenso" e homenageia os navegadores polinésios, que se guiavam pelo céu no Pacífico. A história não para aí: estudos posteriores mostraram que a região é menos massiva do que se pensava e que boa parte do nosso movimento vem de uma concentração maior e mais distante, a de Shapley, rumo à qual o próprio Grande Atrator parece se mover.

fontes.trecho: The Great Attractor is a region of enhanced gravitational attraction in the local universe. It lies in the general direction of the Norma Cluster and the Hydra–Centaurus Supercluster, approximately 150–250 million light-years from the Milky Way. Its presence was inferred from the peculiar motions of galaxies, which deviate from the motion expected solely from the expansion of the universe. [...] The region is difficult to observe at visible wavelengths because it lies behind the galactic plane of the Milky Way, within the Zone of Avoidance. Dust, gas, and foreground stars obscure many background galaxies in this part of the sky. Astronomers therefore study the area using X-ray, radio, infrared, and neutral-hydrogen observations, which penetrate the obscuring material more effectively than visible light. The Great Attractor was incorporated into the definition of the Laniakea Supercluster in 2014. [...] These departures are known as peculiar velocities and result mainly from gravitational interactions with nearby concentrations and deficits of matter. [...] The Great Attractor was identified during the 1980s by a collaboration informally known as the Seven Samurai: David Burstein, Roger Davies, Alan Dressler, Sandra Faber, Donald Lynden-Bell, Roberto Terlevich, and Gary Wegner. The group studied approximately 400 elliptical galaxies using the Dn–sigma relation [...] By comparing distance estimates with observed redshifts, the researchers constructed maps of the galaxies' peculiar velocities. The resulting pattern showed a coherent stream of galaxies toward a previously unrecognized concentrat [...] The Great Attractor is itself moving generally toward Shapley rather than acting as the ultimate endpoint of all nearby flows. [...] Its results indicated that the Norma region was  much less massive than some early estimates and that a substantial part of the Local Group's motion is produced by more distant structures, especially the Shapley Supercluster.

The Laniakea Supercluster or Laniakea for short (; Hawaiian lit. 'immense heaven') is the large-scale structure centered around the Great Attractor that is home to the Milky Way and approximately 100,000 other nearby galaxies. It was originally defined in September 2014 as a galaxy supercluster [...] published a new way of defining superclusters according to the relative velocities of galaxies as basins of attraction. [...] The name was suggested by Nawaʻa Napoleon, an associate professor of Hawaiian language at Kapiʻolani Community College. The name honors Polynesian navigators, who used knowledge of the sky to navigate the Pacific Ocean. [...] influences the motions of the Local Group of galaxies, where the Milky Way galaxy resides, and all others throughout the supercluster.

gancho: Astrônomos acharam uma galáxia que parece ter pouquíssima ou nenhuma matéria escura. Paradoxalmente, isso pode ajudar a provar que a matéria escura existe.
explicacao: A galáxia NGC 1052-DF2 é do tipo ultradifuso: grande, espalhada e muito tênue. Foi a primeira proposta de uma galáxia praticamente sem matéria escura, a massa invisível que se considerava necessária para formar galáxias. Uma das alternativas à matéria escura é que o efeito atribuído a ela seja, na verdade, um comportamento ainda desconhecido da gravidade da matéria comum. Se fosse assim, esse efeito teria de aparecer em qualquer galáxia, inclusive nesta. Uma galáxia sem ele sugere que a matéria escura é algo separado, que pode estar presente ou faltar. A descoberta foi contestada: em 2019, uma equipe do Instituto de Astrofísica de Canárias calculou que ela estaria a 42 milhões de anos-luz, e não a 64 milhões, o que abriria espaço para matéria escura, como em qualquer outra galáxia. Medições posteriores com o Hubble, porém, confirmaram a distância maior, e em junho de 2021 novas observações reforçaram que ela tem pouca matéria escura. Depois surgiram uma segunda galáxia parecida no mesmo grupo, a NGC 1052-DF4, e uma terceira, a FCC 224, em 2025. Ainda são necessários mais estudos para confirmar o que isso significa.

fontes.trecho: NGC 1052-DF2 is an ultra diffuse galaxy (UDG) identified in a wide-field imaging survey of the NGC 1052 group by the Dragonfly Telephoto Array. It has been proposed that the galaxy contains little or no dark matter, the first such discovery. On 20 March 2019, a follow-up study announcing the discovery of a second UDG lacking dark matter, NGC 1052-DF4, was published. [...] On 3 June 2019, however, a separate team used a full observing dataset on the same object to review this claim. Using five independent methods to estimate distances of heavenly bodies, a team of researchers from the Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias (IAC) found the distance of NGC 1052-DF2 to be 42 million light years (13 MPc), not some 64 million light years (19 MPc) from the Earth. [...] This implied a significant part of NGC 1052-DF2 could be made up of dark matter, like any other galaxy. However, follow-up observations using Hubble Space Telescope Advanced Camera for Surveys imaging measured the tip of the red-giant branch distance to NGC 1052-DF2, which IAC researchers detected at 13 Mpc, to be 22.1±1.2 Mpc, consistent with earlier surface brightness fluctuation measurements. [...] The apparent lack of dark matter in NGC 1052-DF2 may help prove that dark matter is real: If what appears to be dark matter is really just a currently unknown effect of the gravity of ordinary matter then this apparent dark matter should also appear in this galaxy. Further study will be needed before this and any other possible implications can be confirmed. If confirmed, the absence of dark matter may also have implications for theories of galaxy formation, as dark matter has been thought to be needed for galaxy formation. [...] In June 2021 further observations by Hubble have confirmed NGC 1052-DF2 as deficient in dark matter. [...] Astronomers discovered a second galaxy with no dark matter, NGC 1052-DF4, which is another ultra diffuse galaxy - quite large, spread-out, and faint to observe. [...] A third galaxy without dark matter was identified in 2025, FCC 224.

gancho: O Objeto de Hoag é um anel quase perfeito de estrelas azuis em volta de um núcleo amarelo, e não se sabe como se formou. E, pelo vão entre os dois, aparece outra galáxia em anel, bem mais distante.
explicacao: Arthur Hoag o descobriu em 1950 e ficou na dúvida entre uma nebulosa planetária e uma galáxia peculiar. Ele chegou a propor que o anel fosse um efeito de lente gravitacional, a luz de algo mais distante entortada pela gravidade. A ideia caiu porque o núcleo e o anel têm o mesmo desvio para o vermelho e porque telescópios melhores mostraram que o anel é cheio de nós, o que uma lente não produziria. A galáxia fica a cerca de 600 milhões de anos-luz, e o anel tem por volta de 121 mil anos-luz de diâmetro externo. As galáxias em anel "clássicas" surgem quando uma galáxia pequena atravessa uma maior, em forma de disco, e cria uma onda que se espalha como um anel. No Objeto de Hoag, porém, não há sinal da segunda galáxia que teria servido de "projétil", nem dos fragmentos que um choque deixaria, embora talvez já tenham sumido se a colisão ocorreu há mais de 3 bilhões de anos. Outra proposta, a de uma instabilidade numa galáxia com barra, também é contestada. Algumas galáxias têm anéis parecidos, mas nenhuma com a mesma simetria. E a galáxia em anel vista pelo vão é outra raridade, já que galáxias em anel são incomuns.

fontes.trecho: Hoag's Object is an unusual ring galaxy in the constellation of Serpens Caput. It is named after Arthur Hoag, who discovered it in 1950 and identified it as either a planetary nebula or a peculiar galaxy. [...] A nearly perfect ring of young hot blue stars circles the older yellow nucleus of this ring galaxy c. 600 million light-years away in the constellation Serpens. [...] and an outer 45″ diameter of 121±4 kly (39.9±1.7 kpc). [...] Though ring galaxies are rare, another more distant ring galaxy can be seen through Hoag's Object, between the nucleus and the outer ring of the galaxy [...] A few other galaxies share the primary characteristics of Hoag's Object, including a bright detached ring of stars [...] While none match Hoag's Object in symmetry, these galaxies are sometimes called Hoag-type galaxies. [...] In the initial announcement of his discovery, Hoag proposed the hypothesis that the visible ring was a product of gravitational lensing. This idea was later discarded because the nucleus and the ring have the same redshift, and because more advanced telescopes revealed the ring's knotty structure, which would not be visible if the galaxy were a product of gravitational lensing. Many of the galaxy's details remain mysterious, foremost of which is how it formed. So-called "classic" ring galaxies are generally formed by the collision of a small galaxy with a larger disk-shaped galaxy, producing a density wave in the disk that leads to a characteristic ring-like appearance. [...] However, there is no sign of any second galaxy that would have acted as the "bullet" [...] Observations with one of the most sensitive telescopes have also failed to uncover any faint galaxy fragments that should be observable in a collision scenario. However, a team of scientists that analyzes the galaxy admits that "if the carnage happened more than 3 billion years ago, there might not be any detritus left to see." Noah Brosch suggested that Hoag's Object might be a product of an extreme "bar instability" that occurred a few billion years ago in a barred spiral galaxy. Schweizer et al. claim this is an unlikely hypothesis

gancho: O primeiro quasar foi achado com a ajuda da Lua: medições feitas quando ela passou na frente de uma fonte de rádio deram sua posição. Lá havia uma "estrela" que, na verdade, estava a bilhões de anos-luz.
explicacao: Nos anos 1950, levantamentos de rádio acharam fontes pequenas sem nenhum objeto visível que correspondesse a elas. Em 1960, centenas já estavam no Terceiro Catálogo de Cambridge, e os astrônomos procuravam suas contrapartes no céu. Uma delas, a 3C 273, passaria cinco vezes por trás da Lua. Cyril Hazard e John Bolton aproveitaram uma dessas ocultações para medi-la com o radiotelescópio de Parkes, na Austrália, e assim Maarten Schmidt pôde achar o objeto visível e obter seu espectro com o telescópio Hale, de 200 polegadas. As linhas estranhas eram linhas comuns de hidrogênio, desviadas 15,8% para o vermelho. Se o desvio viesse do movimento do "astro", ele se afastaria a uns 47 mil km/s, muito além de qualquer estrela. Se viesse da expansão do universo, o objeto estaria muito longe e seria brilhante como nada conhecido. Schmidt e Bev Oke publicaram os resultados em 1963, mas a ideia demorou a ser aceita, porque ninguém sabia o que geraria tanta energia. Hoje se sabe que um quasar é o núcleo de uma galáxia alimentado por um buraco negro supermassivo. O 3C 273 brilha uns 4 trilhões de vezes mais que o Sol em luz visível e ofusca em mais de 16 vezes a galáxia que o abriga.

fontes.trecho: because they were first identified during the 1950s as sources of radio-wave emission of unknown physical origin [...] They were first noted as radio sources with no corresponding visible object. [...] By 1960, hundreds of these objects had been recorded and published in the Third Cambridge Catalogue while astronomers scanned the skies for their optical counterparts. [...] Another radio source, 3C 273, was predicted to undergo five occultations by the Moon. Measurements taken by Cyril Hazard and John Bolton during one of the occultations using the Parkes Radio Telescope allowed Maarten Schmidt to find a visible counterpart to the radio source and obtain an optical spectrum using the 200-inch (5.1 m) Hale Telescope on Mount Palomar. This spectrum revealed the same strange emission lines. Schmidt was able to demonstrate that these were likely to be the ordinary spectral lines of hydrogen redshifted by 15.8% [...] If this was due to the physical motion of the "star", then 3C 273 was receding at an enormous velocity, around 47,000 km/s, far beyond the speed of any known star [...] If the measured redshift was due to relative velocity caused by inflation, then this would support an interpretation of very distant objects with extraordinarily high luminosity and power output, far beyond any object observed to date. [...] Schmidt's explanation for the high redshift was not widely accepted at the time. A major concern was the enormous amount of energy these objects would have to be radiating if they were distant. In the 1960s, no commonly accepted mechanism could account for this. [...] The emission from an AGN is powered by accretion onto a supermassive black hole [...] High-resolution images of quasars, particularly from the Hubble Space Telescope, have shown that quasars occur in the centers of ga

3C 273 is a quasar located at the center of a giant elliptical galaxy in the constellation of Virgo. It was the first quasar ever to be identified and is the visually brightest quasar in the sky as seen from the Earth, with an apparent visual magnitude of 12.9, outshining by more than 16 times the entire galaxy that hosts it. The derived distance to this object is 749 megaparsecs (2.4 billion light-years). [...] the quasar is over 4 trillion times more luminous than the Sun at visible wavelengths. [...] After accurate positions were obtained using lunar occultation by Cyril Hazard at the Parkes Radio Telescope, the radio source was quickly associated with an optical counterpart, an unresolved stellar object. In 1963, Maarten Schmidt and Bev Oke published a pair of papers in Nature reporting that 3C 273 has a substantial redshift of 0.158, placing it several billion light-years away.

gancho: Em 2010, dados públicos de um telescópio de raios gama revelaram duas bolhas gigantes saindo do centro da Via Láctea, de 25 mil anos-luz cada. A principal suspeita é o buraco negro central, mas a origem ainda é debatida.
explicacao: A estrutura toda se estende por 50 mil anos-luz e cobre mais de 100 graus do céu, mais da metade dele, da constelação de Virgem à do Grou. Quem a revelou foi Doug Finkbeiner, do Centro de Astrofísica Harvard-Smithsonian, com os pós-graduandos Meng Su e Tracy Slatyer, processando dados públicos do Large Area Telescope do satélite Fermi, da NASA. As bolhas tinham escapado a estudos anteriores por causa de uma "névoa" de raios gama espalhada pelo céu inteiro, e a equipe só as encontrou depois de subtrair estimativas dessa névoa. Olhando para trás, havia indícios delas em dados de satélites mais antigos, como o ROSAT e o WMAP. As bordas bem definidas sugerem uma liberação de energia grande e relativamente rápida, e as bolhas podem ter milhões de anos. Uma possibilidade é um jato de partículas do buraco negro do centro da galáxia: hoje não há sinal de jato, mas pode ter havido no passado. Outra é um surto de formação de estrelas, já que em outras galáxias esses surtos produzem enormes fluxos de gás. Desde então, simulações de computador, como as de 2022, reforçaram a hipótese de que as bolhas foram infladas por uma fase ativa do buraco negro central, Sagitário A*, embora o tema ainda seja estudado. A descoberta foi comparada, em escala, à de um novo continente na Terra.

fontes.titulo: Astronomers Find Giant, Previously Unseen Structure in our Galaxy (Harvard-Smithsonian CfA)
fontes.trecho: NASA's Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope has unveiled a previously unseen structure centered in the Milky Way -- a finding likened in terms of scale to the discovery of a new continent on Earth. The feature, which spans 50,000 light-years, may be the remnant of an eruption from a supersized black hole at the center of our galaxy. "What we see are two gamma-ray-emitting bubbles that extend 25,000 light-years north and south of the galactic center," said Doug Finkbeiner, an astronomer at the Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics (CfA) in Cambridge, Mass., who first recognized the feature. "We don't fully understand their nature or origin." At more than 100 degrees across, the structure spans more than half of the sky, from the constellation Virgo to the constellation Grus. It may be millions of years old. [...] Finkbeiner and Harvard graduate students Meng Su and Tracy Slatyer revealed the bubbles by processing publicly available data from the satellite's Large Area Telescope (LAT). [...] The structures eluded previous astronomers studying gamma rays due in part to the so-called diffuse emission -- a fog of gamma rays that appears all over the sky. [...] By using various estimates of the gamma-ray fog, including the Fermi team's, Finkbeiner and his colleagues were able to subtract it from the LAT data and unveil the giant bubbles. [...] Taken together, the structure's shape and emissions suggest that it was formed as a result of a large and relatively rapid energy release -- the source of which remains a mystery, Finkbeiner noted. One possibility includes a particle jet from the supermassive black hole at the galactic center. [...] While there is no evidence that the Milky Way's black hole sports such a jet today, it may have in the past. The bubbles also may have formed as a result of gas outflows from a burst of star formation [...] "In other galaxies, we see that starbursts can drive enormous gas outflows," said David Spergel [...] Finkbeiner noted that, in retrospect, hints of the bubbles appear in earlier spacecraft data, including the Germany-led Roentgen X-ray Satellite (ROSAT) and NASA's Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropy Probe (WMAP).

In November 2010, it was announced that two large elliptical lobe structures of energetic plasma, termed bubbles, which emit gamma- and X-rays, were detected astride the Milky Way galaxy's core. [...] The origin of the bubbles is being researched. [...] By 2022, detailed computer simulations further confirmed that the bubbles were caused by the Sagittarius A* black hole.

gancho: O primeiro planeta achado em volta de uma estrela como o Sol, em 1995, contrariava as teorias: um gigante com metade da massa de Júpiter que circula a estrela em uns quatro dias, mais perto dela que Mercúrio do Sol.
explicacao: Em outubro de 1995, Michel Mayor e Didier Queloz, da Universidade de Genebra, anunciaram na revista Nature um planeta em volta de 51 Pegasi, estrela parecida com o Sol a cerca de 50 anos-luz. Eles não viram o planeta. Com um espectrógrafo sensível, perceberam que as linhas do espectro da estrela oscilavam com regularidade, num vaivém de uns 70 metros por segundo, provocado pela gravidade de algo a apenas 7 milhões de quilômetros dela. Em uma semana, outra equipe, do Observatório Lick, confirmou o achado. O espantoso era o lugar: um mundo enorme tão colado na estrela não cabia nas teorias de formação de planetas da época e foi tratado como anomalia. Depois surgiram muitos outros "Júpiteres quentes", e os astrônomos passaram a estudar a migração de órbitas para explicá-los. A descoberta rendeu o Nobel de Física de 2019. Houve um quase precursor: um planeta em Gamma Cephei, sugerido em 1988 por uma equipe canadense, teve o anúncio retirado em 1992 por dados insuficientes e só foi confirmado em 2003. Desde 1995, a lista não parou de crescer: em setembro de 2025, a contagem oficial da NASA chegou a 6.000 exoplanetas, com mais de 8.000 candidatos à espera de confirmação.

fontes.trecho: Dimidium was the first exoplanet to be discovered orbiting a main-sequence star, the Sun-like 51 Pegasi [...] is an extrasolar planet approximately 50 light-years (15 parsecs) away [...] The exoplanet's discovery was announced on October 6, 1995, by Michel Mayor and Didier Queloz of the University of Geneva in the journal Nature. [...] For this discovery, they were awarded the 2019 Nobel Prize in Physics. The planet was discovered using a sensitive spectroscope that could detect the slight and regular velocity changes in the star's spectral lines of around 70 metres per second. These changes are caused by the planet's gravitational effects from just 7 million kilometres' distance from the star. Within a week of the announcement, the planet was confirmed by another team using the Lick Observatory in California. [...] It was discovered that the planet orbits the star in around four days. It is much closer to it than Mercury is to the Sun, moves at an orbital speed of 136 km/s (300,000 mph), yet has a minimum mass about half that of Jupiter (about 150 times that of the Earth). At the time, the presence of a huge world so close to its star was not compatible with theories of planet formation and was considered an anomaly. However, since then, numerous other "hot Jupiters" have been discovered (such as those orbiting 55 Cancri and τ Boötis), and astronomers are revising their theories of planet formation to account for them by studying orbital migration.

The first indications of γ Cephei Ab were reported in July 1988. The planet was tentatively identified by a Canadian team of astronomers, which was led by Bruce Campbell, Gordon Walker and Stephenson Yang [...] However, the claim was retracted in 1992 due to the quality of the data not being good enough to make a solid discovery. [...] On 7 May 2003, γ Cephei Ab was finally confirmed.

fontes.titulo: NASA's Tally of Planets Outside Our Solar System Reaches 6,000 (NASA, 2025)
fontes.trecho: Sep 17, 2025 [...] The official number of exoplanets — planets outside our solar system — tracked by NASA has reached 6,000. [...] There are more than 8,000 additional candidate planets awaiting confirmation

gancho: Por uma década, muitos astrônomos aceitaram que a Estrela de Barnard tinha planetas gigantes. Era ilusão: o sinal coincidia com ajustes na lente do telescópio. Planetas de verdade só foram achados em 2024 e 2025.
explicacao: Peter van de Kamp observava a Estrela de Barnard desde 1938 no Observatório Sproul, do Swarthmore College, nos Estados Unidos. Ele buscava, em chapas fotográficas, desvios de um micrômetro na posição da estrela, que denunciariam a gravidade de um planeta puxando-a. Para evitar erros pessoais, até dez pessoas mediam as chapas e tiravam a média. De 1963 a cerca de 1973, boa parte dos astrônomos aceitou a conclusão dele: havia ali um ou mais planetas com massa comparável à de Júpiter. Em 1973, dois trabalhos derrubaram a ideia. George Gatewood e Heinrich Eichhorn, em outro observatório e com técnicas mais novas, não acharam o sinal. E John Hershey, com dados do próprio Swarthmore, mostrou que os desvios de várias estrelas coincidiam com as datas de manutenção e modificação da lente objetiva do telescópio. Van de Kamp nunca admitiu o erro, voltou a anunciar dois planetas em 1982 e morreu em 1995. Uma super-Terra anunciada em 2018 também caiu: o sinal vinha da atividade da própria estrela. Só em 2024, com o espectrógrafo ESPRESSO, do Very Large Telescope, surgiu a primeira evidência convincente de um planeta ali. Em 2025, outra equipe confirmou quatro, todos com menos massa que a Terra e em órbitas apertadas.

fontes.trecho: Barnard's Star hosts a system of four close-orbiting, sub-Earth-mass planets (Barnard's Star b, c, d & e). Multiple claims for a planetary system had been proposed since the beginning of the twentieth century, notably by Peter van de Kamp in the 1960s, but none were supported by follow-up studies, until the now known four-planet system was discovered by two independent teams of astronomers in 2024–2025. [...] In August 2024, by using data from ESPRESSO spectrograph of the Very Large Telescope, the existence of an exoplanet with a minimum mass of 0.37±0.05 M🜨 and orbital period of 3.15 days was confirmed. This constituted the first convincing evidence for a planet orbiting Barnard's Star. [...] In March 2025, an independent follow-up study led by Ritvik Basant confirmed all four planets. [...] For a decade from 1963 to about 1973, a substantial number of astronomers accepted a claim by Peter van de Kamp that he had detected, by using astrometry, a perturbation in the proper motion of Barnard's Star consistent with its having one or more planets comparable in mass with Jupiter. Van de Kamp had been observing the star from 1938, attempting, with colleagues at the Sproul Observatory at Swarthmore College, to find minuscule variations of one micrometre in its position on photographic plates consistent with orbital perturbations that would indicate a planetary companion; this involved as many as ten people averaging their results in looking at plates, to avoid systemic individual errors. [...] Other astronomers subsequently repeated Van de Kamp's measurements, and two papers in 1973 undermined the claim of a planet or planets. George Gatewood and Heinrich Eichhorn, at a different observatory and using newer plate measuring techniques, failed to verify the planetary companion. Another paper published by John L. Hershey four months earlier, also using the Swarthmore observatory, found that changes in the astrometric field of various stars correlated to the timing of adjustments and modifications that had been carried out on the refractor telescope's objective lens; the claimed planet was attributed to an artifact of maintenance and upgrade work. [...] Van de Kamp never acknowledged any error and published a further claim of two planets' existence as late as 1982; he died in 1995. [...] However, the existence of the planet was refuted in 2021, when the radial velocity signal was found to originate from long-term activity on the star itself, related to its rotation. [...] In November 2018, a candidate super-Earth planetary companion was reported to orbit Barnard's Star.

gancho: A evidência mais antiga conhecida de um sistema planetário fora do nosso foi registrada em 1917, numa chapa de vidro, e passou quase um século num arquivo sem que ninguém percebesse seu valor. Foi reconhecida em 2016.
explicacao: A chapa, guardada no arquivo dos Observatórios Carnegie, foi feita por Walter Adams no Observatório Mount Wilson, na Califórnia. Ela registra o espectro da estrela de van Maanen, uma anã branca descoberta naquele mesmo ano pelo astrônomo holandês-americano Adriaan van Maanen. No envelope, a anotação dizia apenas que a estrela parecia um pouco mais quente que o Sol. O valor da chapa só apareceu quando o astrônomo Jay Farihi, da University College London, pediu para examiná-la ao escrever uma revisão sobre sistemas planetários em volta de anãs brancas. O espectro mostra linhas de absorção de elementos pesados, como cálcio, magnésio e ferro. Numa anã branca, eles deveriam ter afundado para o interior da estrela por causa do peso. Se continuam na superfície, algo os repõe: hoje se entende que são detritos de corpos rochosos caindo sobre a estrela, as chamadas "anãs brancas poluídas". Segundo Farihi, os anéis de detritos e essa queda exigem a gravidade de planetas de verdade. Foi uma surpresa, porque anãs brancas são estrelas como o Sol no fim da vida, e não se esperava que ainda tivessem material planetário em volta. O planeta em si continua difícil de ver: em 2016 nenhum havia sido detectado ali, e em 2022 surgiu um candidato.

fontes.titulo: 1917 Astronomical Plate Has First-Ever Evidence of Exoplanetary System (Carnegie Science, 2016)
fontes.trecho: it turns out that a 1917 image on an astronomical glass plate from our Carnegie Observatories’ collection shows the first-ever evidence of a planetary system beyond our own Sun. This unexpected find was recognized in the process of researching an article about planetary systems surrounding white dwarf stars in New Astronomy Reviews. [...] the review’s author, Jay Farihi of University College London, contacted our Observatories’ Director, John Mulchaey. He was looking for a plate in the Carnegie archive that contained a spectrum of van Maanen’s star, a white dwarf discovered by Dutch-American astronomer Adriaan van Maanen in the very year our own plate was made. [...] As requested, the Observatories located the 1917 plate, made by former Observatories Director Walter Adams at Mount Wilson Observatory, which was then part of Carnegie. Other than a notation on the plate’s sleeve indicating that the star looked a bit warmer than our own Sun, everything seemed very ordinary. [...] Carnegie’s 1917 spectrum of van Maanen’s star revealed the presence of heavier elements, such as calcium, magnesium, and iron, which should have long since disappeared into the star's interior due to their weight. [...] These recently discovered systems are called “polluted white dwarfs.” They were a surprise to astronomers, because white dwarfs are stars like our own Sun at the end of their lifetimes, so it was not at all expected that they would have leftover planetary material around them at that stage. [...] Planets themselves have not yet been detected orbiting van Maanen's star, nor around similar systems, but Farihi is confident it is only a matter of time. "The mechanism that creates the rings of planetary debris, and the deposition onto the stellar atmosphere, requires the gravitational influence of full-fledged planets,” he explained.

In 2016, it was discovered that a spectrographic plate of the star made in 1917 gives evidence—the earliest known—of planetary matter outside the Solar System, in the form of calcium absorption lines that indicate the presence of planetary material polluting the stellar atmosphere. [...] Instead, the surface of the star was likely strewn with circumstellar material, such as from the remains of one or more rocky, terrestrial planets. [...] As of 2022, a candidate planet was detected via astrometry, with a mass between 0.4 and 1.1 Jupiter masses.

gancho: Com duas rodas de reação quebradas, o telescópio Kepler não conseguia mais mirar. A solução foi usar a pressão da luz do Sol como "terceira roda". E o Sol é também o principal suspeito de ter estragado as rodas.
explicacao: Lançado em 2009, o Kepler ficava apontado para um trecho do céu na constelação do Cisne, vigiando cerca de 150 mil estrelas à espera das pequenas quedas de brilho causadas por planetas passando na frente delas. Para mirar com precisão, usava rodas de reação, peças parecidas com giroscópios, e precisava de três funcionando. Uma parou em julho de 2012; a segunda, em maio de 2013. O problema é que a própria luz solar empurra a nave: os fótons batem nela e exercem pressão, e sem a terceira roda não havia como compensar isso em todas as direções. Os engenheiros transformaram o empurrão em aliado. Deixaram a nave quase paralela à sua trajetória em volta do Sol, de modo que a pressão da luz a mantivesse estável, como um caiaque que segue reto apontado para a correnteza. Nasceu assim a missão K2, que passou a observar campos perto da eclíptica, trocando de região a cada cerca de três meses. A equipe estimava fazer 10 dessas campanhas com o combustível restante; chegou a 19. Uma análise posterior ligou as falhas a corrosão nos rolamentos de aço por arcos elétricos, que seriam provocados por ejeções de massa coronal do Sol. Os testes mostram que o mecanismo é possível, mas dificilmente será provado que foi isso o que aconteceu no Kepler.

fontes.trecho: Launched on March 6, 2009, the Kepler space telescope combined cutting-edge techniques [...] Originally positioned to stare continuously at 150,000 stars in one star-studded patch of the sky in the constellation Cygnus [...] Kepler detected planets by observing transits, or tiny dips in the brightness of a star that occur when a planet crosses in front of the star. [...] In May 2013, the Kepler spacecraft lost the second of four gyroscope-like reaction wheels, which are used to precisely point the spacecraft, effectively ending new data collection for the original mission. The spacecraft required three functioning wheels to position the telescope [...] also pushes the spacecraft around by the pressure exerted when the photons of sunlight strike the spacecraft. Without a third wheel to help counteract the solar pressure, the spacecraft's ultra-precise pointing capability could not be controlled in all directions. [...] So engineers came up with a clever scheme. They gave the spacecraft a new lease on life by using the pressure of sunlight to maintain its pointing, like a kayak steering into the current. [...] along the ecliptic plane. This extended mission required the spacecraft to shift its field of view to new portions of the sky roughly every three months in what the team referred to as a [...] Initially, the Kepler team estimated that the K2 mission could conduct 10 campaigns with the remaining fuel; it reached 19.

fontes.titulo: Kepler's Second Light: How K2 Will Work (NASA, 2013)
fontes.trecho: This technique of using the sun as the "third wheel" could have Kepler on the hunt for planets again, soon. [...] To achieve the necessary stability, the orientation of the spacecraft must be nearly parallel to its orbital path around the sun

on July 14, 2012, one of the four reaction wheels used for pointing the spacecraft stopped turning [...] Then, on May 11, 2013, a second one failed [...] The reaction wheel failures were traced back to pitting caused by arcing between the steel ball bearings in the reaction wheel. The arcing was in turn caused by coronal mass ejections (CMEs) from the sun.

fontes.titulo: Do Space Probes Fail Because Of Space Weather? (Hackaday, 2018)
fontes.trecho: As it turns out, the failures of reaction wheels, specifically on the FUSE and Kepler missions, was correlated with space weather, specifically coronal mass ejections (CMEs) from the Sun. These CMEs induce a voltage across the bearings and the bearing races in the reaction wheels, and after testing, these researchers discovered it doesn’t take much to generate a small arc from the bearing to the bearing race. This arc causes a small bit of pitting, which over time increases the friction on the reaction wheels, eventually causing it to fail. [...] While the researchers provide the experimental data showing that bearings can fail due to a voltage across a bearing and a race, it’s unlikely we’ll ever be able to prove Kepler, FUSE, or Dawn suffered a reaction wheel failure because of space weather.

gancho: Para vermos um planeta como a Terra passar diante da sua estrela, a órbita dele tem de estar alinhada com a nossa linha de visão. A chance é de só 0,47%. Ainda assim, o Kepler mostrou que há mais planetas que estrelas.
explicacao: O método do trânsito, o mais produtivo da caça a exoplanetas, procura a pequena queda de brilho de uma estrela quando um planeta passa diante dela. Isso só acontece se a órbita estiver quase exatamente de perfil para nós. A probabilidade é a razão entre o diâmetro da estrela e o diâmetro da órbita: cerca de 10% dos planetas com órbitas curtas têm o alinhamento certo, e a fração cai à medida que a órbita cresce. Para um planeta à distância da Terra, em volta de uma estrela do tamanho do Sol, a chance é de 0,47%. Por isso, não ver trânsito nunca prova que uma estrela não tem planetas. E o sinal é minúsculo: um planeta do tamanho da Terra diante de uma estrela como o Sol reduz o brilho em apenas 80 partes por milhão. A saída é estatística. Vigiando milhares ou centenas de milhares de estrelas ao mesmo tempo, os levantamentos de trânsito acham mais planetas que outros métodos. O Kepler, somando suas duas missões, examinou mais de 500 mil estrelas. Mesmo enxergando só os poucos sistemas vistos de perfil, os dados levaram a NASA a concluir que o céu noturno tem mais planetas do que estrelas.

fontes.trecho: First, planetary transits are observable only when the planet's orbit happens to be perfectly aligned from the astronomers' vantage point. The probability of a planetary orbital plane being directly on the line-of-sight to a star is the ratio of the diameter of the star to the diameter of the orbit (in small stars, the radius of the planet is also an important factor). About 10% of planets with small orbits have such an alignment, and the fraction decreases for planets with larger orbits. For a planet orbiting a Sun-sized star at 1 AU, the probability of a random alignment producing a transit is 0.47%. Therefore, the method cannot guarantee that any particular star is not a host to planets. However, by scanning large areas of the sky containing thousands or even hundreds of thousands of stars at once, transit surveys can find more extrasolar planets than the radial-velocity method.
Because a decrease in brightness from an Earth-sized planet transiting a Sun-like star is so small, only 80 ppm
They proved that our night sky is filled with more planets than even stars [...] K2 lasted as long as the first mission and bumped Kepler's count of surveyed stars up to more than 500,000.

gancho: A 63 anos-luz há um planeta azul-cobalto, como a Terra vista do espaço. Mas o azul não vem de oceanos, e sim de nuvens com partículas de silicato. E lá talvez chova vidro de lado, com ventos de milhares de km/h.
explicacao: Em 2013, o telescópio Hubble mediu a cor real de HD 189733b, um gigante gasoso em volta de outra estrela. O truque foi comparar a luz do sistema antes, durante e depois de o planeta passar por trás da estrela. Quando ele se escondeu, faltou luz no azul, mas não no verde nem no vermelho: o objeto que sumiu era azul. A cor viria de uma atmosfera enevoada e escaldante, com nuvens altas cheias de partículas de silicato. No calor, os silicatos podem se condensar em gotinhas minúsculas de vidro, que espalham mais a luz azul do que a vermelha. Daí a imagem, que a própria NASA apresenta como possibilidade, de chuva de vidro soprada de lado. O planeta é um "Júpiter quente" tão perto da estrela que tem sempre a mesma face voltada para ela: um lado vive de dia e o outro de noite. Em 2007, o telescópio Spitzer fez um dos primeiros mapas de temperatura de um exoplaneta, e a diferença entre os dois lados deve alimentar ventos ferozes. Pesquisadores da Universidade de Warwick estimaram rajadas de até 8.700 km/h, do lado do dia para o da noite.

fontes.titulo: NASA Hubble Finds a True Blue Planet (NASA, 2013)
fontes.trecho: Jul 11, 2013 [...] Astronomers making visible-light observations with NASA's Hubble Space Telescope have deduced the actual color of a planet orbiting another star 63 light-years away. [...] Hubble's Space Telescope Imaging Spectrograph measured changes in the color of light from the planet before, during and after a pass behind its star. [...] "We saw the light becoming less bright in the blue but not in the green or red. Light was missing in the blue but not in the red when it was hidden," [...] "This means that the object that disappeared was blue." [...] If seen directly, this planet would look like a deep blue dot, reminiscent of Earth's color as seen from space. [...] and it possibly rains glass – sideways – in howling, 4,500-mph winds. The cobalt blue color comes not from the reflection of a tropical ocean as it does on Earth, but rather a hazy, blow-torched atmosphere containing high clouds laced with silicate particles. Silicates condensing in the heat could form very small drops of glass that scatter blue light more than red light. [...] HD 189733b is among a bizarre class of planets called hot Jupiters [...] so close that it is gravitationally locked. One side always faces the star and the other side is always dark. In 2007, NASA's Spitzer Space Telescope measured the infrared light, or heat, from the planet, leading to one of the first temperature maps for an exoplanet. [...] This should cause fierce winds to roar from the day side to the night side.
Scientists at the University of Warwick determined that HD 189733 b has winds of up to 8,700 km/h (5,400 mph) blowing from the day side to the night side.

gancho: Em 2011, astrônomos estimaram que o planeta TrES-2b reflete menos de 1% da luz que recebe: é mais escuro que carvão e que tinta acrílica preta. E admitiram não saber o que o deixava tão negro.
explicacao: TrES-2b é um gigante gasoso do tamanho de Júpiter, a cerca de 750 anos-luz, na direção da constelação do Dragão. Júpiter é envolto em nuvens claras de amônia, que refletem mais de um terço da luz do Sol que chega até ele. TrES-2b fica tão perto da sua estrela que passa de 1.800 °F (quase mil graus Celsius), quente demais para essas nuvens. Sua atmosfera deve conter substâncias que absorvem luz, como sódio e potássio vaporizados ou óxido de titânio gasoso. Mas, segundo os autores, nenhuma delas explica por completo um negrume tão extremo. A medição foi feita com dados do telescópio Kepler. Como a Lua, o planeta mostra fases enquanto gira em volta da estrela, e isso faz o brilho total do sistema oscilar um pouco. Acompanhando mais de 50 órbitas, a equipe de David Kipping detectou a menor variação de brilho já medida num exoplaneta até então, de apenas 6 partes por milhão. Um mundo mais refletor produziria oscilações maiores. Se toda essa oscilação viesse de luz refletida, o planeta refletiria 2,53%; mas, como boa parte dela parece ser brilho próprio do calor, a estimativa caiu para menos de 1%. Ele não é totalmente preto, porém: de tão quente, emite um fraco brilho avermelhado, como uma brasa ou a resistência de um fogão elétrico.

fontes.titulo: Alien World Is Blacker Than Coal (Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics, 2011)
fontes.trecho: Astronomers have discovered the darkest known exoplanet - a distant, Jupiter-sized gas giant known as TrES-2b. Their measurements show that TrES-2b reflects less than one percent of the sunlight falling on it, making it blacker than coal or any planet or moon in our solar system. "TrES-2b is considerably less reflective than black acrylic paint, so it's truly an alien world," said astronomer David Kipping [...] In our solar system, Jupiter is swathed in bright clouds of ammonia that reflect more than a third of the sunlight reaching it. [...] The star's intense light heats TrES-2b to a temperature of more than 1,800° Fahrenheit - much too hot for ammonia clouds. Instead, its exotic atmosphere contains light-absorbing chemicals like vaporized sodium and potassium, or gaseous titanium oxide. Yet none of these chemicals fully explain the extreme blackness of TrES-2b. "It's not clear what is responsible for making this planet so extraordinarily dark," stated co-author David Spiegel of Princeton University. "However, it's not completely pitch black. It's so hot that it emits a faint red glow, much like a burning ember or the coils on an electric stove." Kipping and Spiegel determined the reflectivity of TrES-2b using data from NASA's Kepler spacecraft. [...] And like our moon, the planet shows changing phases as it orbits its star. This causes the total brightness of the star plus planet to vary slightly. "By combining the impressive precision from Kepler with observations of over 50 orbits, we detected the smallest-ever change in brightness from an exoplanet: just 6 parts per million," said Kipping. [...] A more reflective world would have shown larger brightness variations as its phase changed. [...] located about 750 light-years away in the direction of the constellation Draco.

The planet was identified in 2011 as the darkest known exoplanet, reflecting less than 1% of any light that hits it. Reflecting less light than charcoal, on the surface the planet is said to be pitch black, although it does  emit dim red glow due to its temperature. [...] If the entire day–night contrast were due to geometric albedo, it would be 2.53%, but modeling suggests that much of this is dayside emission due to the planet's high temperature and the true albedo is much lower. It is estimated to be less than 1%

gancho: Em volta da estrela Kepler-51 há planetas quase do tamanho de Júpiter, mas com só algumas vezes a massa da Terra. São tão pouco densos que foram apelidados de planetas "algodão-doce", e não se sabe bem por quê.
explicacao: Os três planetas internos do sistema, Kepler-51b, c e d, são chamados de superinflados: têm raio comparável ao de gigantes gasosos, mas massa só algumas vezes maior que a da Terra. O mais inflado, Kepler-51d, tem 9,32 vezes o raio da Terra, quase o tamanho de Saturno, mas massa de só algumas vezes a dela. Isso dá uma densidade de 0,0381 grama por centímetro cúbico, muito abaixo da de qualquer planeta do Sistema Solar. Em 2019, o Hubble tentou procurar água na atmosfera de Kepler-51b e 51d, observando a luz da estrela atravessar o ar desses planetas durante a passagem deles. Os espectros saíram sem nenhuma assinatura, o que sugere uma camada alta de névoa. A equipe concluiu que a baixa densidade se deve em parte à juventude do sistema, de uns 500 milhões de anos, e os modelos indicam que os planetas se formaram além da "linha de neve" da estrela e depois migraram para dentro, como uma fileira de vagões de trem. Com o tempo, devem encolher e perder parte da atmosfera. Ainda assim, o motivo de densidades tão baixas continua indefinido: várias hipóteses foram propostas, e todas têm falhas. Em 2024, o telescópio Webb revelou um quarto planeta no sistema.

fontes.trecho: Kepler-51 is a Sun-like star that is about 500 million years old. It is orbited by four planets—Kepler-51b, c, d and e—first three of which are super-puffs and have the lowest known densities of any known exoplanet. The transiting planets in the system (b, c and d) are similar in radius to gas giants like Jupiter, but have unusually small masses for their size, only a few times greater than Earth's. [...] The reason for the low density of these planets remains elusive, and many hypotheses have been proposed to explain the nature of these planets, all of which have flaws. In 2024, the Kepler-51 system was revealed to have a new planet, detected using transit timing variations by the James Webb Space Telescope and named Kepler-51e. [...] This translates to a very low density of 0.06 g/cm3, much lower than that of any planet in the Solar System. [...] Over time, the planet will contract, lose part of its atmosphere and become a sub-Neptune. [...] Kepler-51d is the puffiest planet in the system, with an density of just 0.0381 g/cm3. It is also the largest planet orbiting Kepler-51, with 9.32 times Earth's radius (59,400 km), almost the same size as Saturn.

Hubble Probes Cotton Candy Planets [...] 23 December 2019 [...] How and why their atmospheres balloon outwards remains unknown, but this feature makes super-puffs prime targets for atmospheric investigation. Using Hubble, the team went looking for evidence of components, notably water, in the atmospheres of Kepler-51b and 51d. [...] The team concluded that the low densities of these planets are in part a consequence of the young age of the system, a mere 500 million years old. Models suggest these planets formed outside of the star’s “snow line” where icy materials can survive. The planets then migrated inward, like a string of railroad cars.

gancho: O planeta WASP-12b está caindo em espiral na sua estrela. A cada ano, a volta dele fica uns 29 milésimos de segundo mais curta, e a estimativa é que seja engolido em cerca de 3,16 milhões de anos.
explicacao: WASP-12b é um "Júpiter quente" descoberto em 2008. Tem cerca de 40% mais massa que Júpiter e dá a volta na estrela em pouco mais de um dia terrestre, a uns 3,5 milhões de quilômetros dela. Tão perto, as forças de maré o esticam num formato alongado e arrancam sua atmosfera, a uma taxa estimada de 6 bilhões de toneladas por segundo. A temperatura passa de 2.500 kelvin.
