Uma camponesa e a neta viram uma figura de traje laranja e capacete branco descer do céu e começaram a recuar com medo. Segundo Gagarin, ele as tranquilizou dizendo que era um cidadão soviético que tinha descido do espaço e precisava de um telefone. O salto tinha peso político: em 1961, as regras da FAI, que homologa recordes aeronáuticos, exigiam que o piloto pousasse junto com a nave. A União Soviética afirmou oficialmente que ele tinha pousado na Vostok, o governo o obrigou a mentir em entrevistas e a FAI homologou os recordes. A verdade só foi admitida em 1971. Mesmo assim, a FAI manteve os recordes e mudou as regras, reconhecendo que o essencial, o lançamento, a órbita e o retorno seguros do piloto, tinha sido cumprido.

fontes.trecho: The Vostok 3KA space capsule was launched from Baikonur Cosmodrome on 12 April 1961, with Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin aboard [...] The flight took 108 minutes from launch to landing. Gagarin parachuted to the ground separately from his capsule after ejecting at 7 km (23,000 ft) altitude. [...] At 07:55 UTC, when Vostok 1 was still 7 km (23,000 ft) from the ground, the hatch of the spacecraft was released, and two seconds later Gagarin was ejected. At 2.5 km (8,200 ft) altitude, the main parachute was deployed from the Vostok spacecraft. Gagarin's parachute opened almost immediately, and about ten minutes later, at 08:05 UTC, Gagarin landed. [...] A kolkhoz woman Annihayat Nurskanova and her granddaughter, Rita, observed the strange scene of a figure in a bright orange suit with a large white helmet landing near them by parachute. Gagarin later recalled, "When they saw me in my space suit and the parachute dragging alongside as I walked, they started to back away in fear. I told them, don't be afraid, I am a Soviet citizen like you, who has descended from space and I must find a telephone to call Moscow!" [...] The FAI rules in 1961 required that a pilot must land with the spacecraft to be considered an official spaceflight for the FAI record books. Although some contemporary Soviet sources stated that Gagarin had parachuted separately to the ground, the Soviet Union officially insisted that he had landed with the Vostok; the government forced the cosmonaut to lie in press conferences, and the FAI certified the flight. The Soviet Union did not admit until 1971 that Gagarin had ejected and landed separately from the Vostok descent module. Gagarin's spaceflight records were nonetheless certified and reaffirmed by the FAI, which revised its rules, and acknowledged that the crucial steps of the safe launch, orbit, and return of the pilot had been accomplished.

gancho: Na primeira caminhada espacial, em 1965, o traje de Alexei Leonov estufou tanto que ele não conseguia voltar para a nave. Ele soltou parte da pressão do traje, abaixo do limite seguro, sem avisar pelo rádio.
explicacao: A Voskhod 2 tinha uma câmara de descompressão inflável, por onde Leonov saiu enquanto o colega Pavel Belyayev ficava na cápsula. A caminhada durou 12 minutos e 9 segundos. No vácuo, o traje Berkut inchou como um balão: Leonov não alcançava nem o disparador da câmera presa ao peito, que ficava na coxa, e no fim o traje estava tão rígido que ele não conseguia entrar de volta na câmara. A saída foi baixar a pressão interna para que as juntas voltassem a dobrar, chegando abaixo dos limites de segurança e flertando com a doença descompressiva. Relatos posteriores dizem que ele ainda entrou de cabeça, contra o procedimento, e ficou entalado de lado ao se virar para fechar a escotilha. Ele não comentou nada disso pelo rádio, para não alarmar ninguém. Os médicos registraram que a temperatura do corpo dele subiu 1,8 °C em 20 minutos, e Leonov contou que o suor chegava aos joelhos dentro do traje. Na época, a agência oficial TASS informou apenas que ele estava bem; a história completa veio de documentos russos divulgados depois da Guerra Fria. Leonov também disse que levava uma pílula de suicídio, para o caso de não conseguir voltar e Belyayev ter de abandoná-lo em órbita.

fontes.trecho: was a Soviet crewed space mission in March 1965. [...] Alexei Leonov became the first person to leave the spacecraft in a specialised spacesuit to conduct a 12-minute spacewalk. [...] Duration: 12 minutes 9 seconds [...] Cosmonaut Alexei Leonov donned a Berkut spacesuit and left the spacecraft while the other cosmonaut of the two-man crew, Pavel Belyayev, remained inside. [...] However, when he tried to use the still camera on his chest, the suit had ballooned and he was unable to reach down to the shutter switch on his leg. After his 12 minutes and 9 seconds outside the Voskhod, Leonov found that his suit had stiffened, due to ballooning out, to the point where he could not re-enter the airlock. He was forced to bleed off some of his suit's pressure, in order to be able to bend the joints, eventually going below safety limits. Leonov did not report his action on the radio to avoid alarming others [...] The government news agency, TASS, reported that, "outside the ship and after returning, Leonov feels well"; however, post-Cold War Russian documents reveal a different story [...] Later accounts report Cosmonaut Leonov violated procedure by entering the airlock head-first, then became stuck sideways when he turned to close the outer hatch, forcing him to flirt with decompression sickness (the "bends") by lowering the suit pressure so he could bend to free himself. Leonov said that he had a suicide pill to swallow had he been unable to re-enter the Voskhod 2, and Belyayev been forced to abandon him in orbit. Doctors reported that Leonov nearly suffered heatstroke — his core body temperature increased by 1.8 °C (3.2 °F) in 20 minutes; Leonov said he was up to his knees in sweat, which sloshed in the suit.

gancho: Os únicos humanos que morreram no espaço foram os três da Soyuz 11, em 1971, quando uma válvula se abriu na volta. Eles só voaram porque um raio X sugeriu tuberculose num membro da equipe titular.
explicacao: A Soyuz 11 levou Georgy Dobrovolsky, Vladislav Volkov e Viktor Patsayev à Salyut 1, a primeira estação espacial do mundo, onde passaram 22 dias, um recorde de permanência na época. A equipe original era outra: Alexei Leonov, Valery Kubasov e Pyotr Kolodin. Quatro dias antes do lançamento, um raio X indicou que Kubasov poderia ter tuberculose, e as regras da missão mandavam trocar a equipe inteira pela reserva. Na volta, os módulos da nave se separavam com parafusos explosivos que deviam disparar em sequência, mas dispararam juntos. O tranco afrouxou uma válvula de equalização de pressão, que se abriu a 168 km de altitude, acima da linha de Kármán. A perda de pressão matou em menos de um minuto, e a válvula ficava embaixo dos assentos, impossível de achar e bloquear a tempo. O corpo de Patsayev estava perto dela; talvez ele tentasse fechá-la quando perdeu a consciência. A cápsula pousou sozinha e, por fora, estava intacta. A equipe de resgate bateu na lateral e ninguém respondeu. Depois do acidente, a Soyuz foi bastante redesenhada para levar só dois cosmonautas, e o espaço extra permitiu que eles usassem trajes pressurizados Sokol no lançamento e no pouso.

fontes.trecho: was the only crewed mission (but failed) to board the world's first space station, Salyut 1. The crew – Georgy Dobrovolsky, Vladislav Volkov, and Viktor Patsayev – arrived at the space station on 7 June 1971, and departed on 29 June 1971. The mission ended in disaster when the crew capsule depressurised during preparations for re-entry, killing the three-person crew. The crew members of Soyuz 11 are the only humans to have died in space (i.e. above the Kármán line). [...] The original prime crew for Soyuz 11 consisted of Alexei Leonov, Valery Kubasov, and Pyotr Kolodin. A medical X-ray examination four days before launch suggested that Kubasov might have tuberculosis, and according to the mission rules, the prime crew was replaced with the backup crew. [...] the cosmonauts remained on board for 22 days, setting space endurance records [...] When the recovery team opened the capsule of the Soyuz 11, they found all three men dead. [...] Outwardly, there was no damage whatsoever. They knocked on the side, but there was no response from within. [...] The two modules were held together by explosive bolts designed to fire sequentially; in fact, they had fired simultaneously. The explosive force of the simultaneous bolt firing caused the internal mechanism of the pressure equalisation valve to loosen a seal [...] The valve opened at an altitude of 168 kilometres (104 mi; 91 nmi), and the resultant loss of pressure was fatal in less than a minute. The valve was located beneath the seats and was impossible to find and block before the air was lost. [...] Patsayev's body was found positioned near the valve, and he may have been attempting to close or block the valve at the time he lost consciousness. [...] The Soyuz spacecraft was extensively redesigned after this incident to carry only two cosmonauts. The extra room meant that the crew could wear Sokol space suits during launch and landing.

gancho: Na descida da Apollo 11, o computador de bordo disparou os alarmes 1202 e 1201: estava sobrecarregado. O pouso seguiu porque o software largava sozinho as tarefas menos importantes e mantinha as vitais.
explicacao: Os alarmes avisavam que o computador tinha ficado sem as áreas de memória de que precisava para rodar as tarefas, e a resposta a eles era um reinício parcial. A culpa era do radar de encontro, que acompanha o módulo de comando em órbita e tinha sido deixado em espera para o caso de um aborto. Um documento de interface falho não exigia sincronia de fase entre duas fontes de 800 Hz, uma do radar e outra usada pelo computador como referência de tempo. Com isso, a antena, parada, parecia tremer sem parar, e o radar roubava do computador 6.400 ciclos de processamento por segundo, cerca de 13% de carga extra sobre os quase 85% habituais nessa fase. Quando Buzz Aldrin pediu uma tela que comparava a altitude medida pelo radar com a calculada, mais 10% de carga estouraram a conta. Mas o software tinha prioridades: a cada reinício, descartava as tarefas menos importantes, inclusive a tela de Aldrin, e preservava a navegação e o controle. Em Houston, o controlador Steve Bales e a equipe dele, que incluía Jack Garman, deram vários "GO", e o pouso deu certo. O problema já tinha sido documentado em testes da Apollo 9, mas, como tinha ocorrido uma só vez, preferiram voar com o equipamento já testado a trocar por um radar novo.

fontes.trecho: PGNCS generated unanticipated warnings during Apollo 11's lunar descent, with the AGC showing a 1202 alarm ("Executive overflow - NO CORE SETS"), and then a 1201 alarm ("Executive overflow - NO VAC AREAS"). The response of the AGC to either alarm was a soft restart. The cause was a rapid, steady stream of spurious cycle steals from the rendezvous radar (tracking the orbiting command module), intentionally left on standby during the descent in case it was needed for an abort. During this part of the approach, the processor would normally be almost 85% loaded. The extra 6,400 cycle steals per second added the equivalent of 13% load, leaving just enough time for all scheduled tasks to run to completion. Five minutes into the descent, Buzz Aldrin gave the computer the command 1668, which instructed it to periodically calculate and display DELTAH (the difference between altitude sensed by the radar and the computed altitude). The 1668 added another 10% to the processor workload, causing executive overflow and a 1202 alarm. [...] The AGC software had been designed with priority scheduling, and automatically recovered, deleting lower priority tasks including the 1668 display task, to complete its critical guidance and control tasks. Guidance controller Steve Bales and his support team that included Jack Garman issued several "GO" calls and the landing was successful. [...] It was caused by a flawed interface control document (ICD) between the PGNCS and the ATCA (Attitude and Translation Control Assembly), that failed to specify phase synchronization between two 800 Hz signals—a problem already known and documented during the launch site testing of LM-3 in Apollo 9. However, because the problem had only occurred once during testing, they concluded that it was safer to fly with the existing hardware that they had already tested, than to fly with a newer but largely untested radar system . In the actual hardware, the position of the rendezvous radar was encoded with synchros excited by a different source of 800 Hz AC than the one used by the computer as a timing reference. The two 800 Hz sources were frequency locked but not phase locked, and the random phase offset made it appear as though the antenna was rapidly "dithering" in position, even though it was completely stationary.

gancho: Quando a estação Skylab caiu sobre a Austrália, em 1979, o condado de Esperance multou a NASA em 400 dólares australianos por jogar lixo. A multa foi paga em 2009, com dinheiro de ouvintes de uma rádio.
explicacao: O Skylab, primeira estação espacial dos EUA, caiu antes do que a NASA esperava. Em 1973, o matemático britânico Desmond King-Hele previu a queda para 1979 por causa do aumento da atividade solar: um Sol mais ativo que o previsto aquece as camadas externas da atmosfera e aumenta o arrasto sobre o que está em órbita. Na reentrada, em julho de 1979, os controladores tentaram mirar o sul do Oceano Índico, com sucesso parcial. A estação não queimou tão rápido quanto se calculava e, por um erro de cálculo de quatro por cento, os destroços caíram em terra, cerca de 480 km a leste de Perth, no oeste da Austrália. Por sorte, era uma área quase desabitada. A queda virou evento de mídia, com apostas sobre hora e local, e um jornal de San Francisco prometeu 10 mil dólares a quem entregasse primeiro um pedaço da estação. Stan Thornton, que achou 24 fragmentos em casa, em Esperance, tirou o primeiro passaporte da vida e voou para buscar o prêmio. O condado de Esperance, em tom de brincadeira, multou a NASA em 400 dólares australianos por jogar lixo. A multa foi cancelada três meses depois, mas em abril de 2009 o radialista Scott Barley arrecadou o valor com os ouvintes do seu programa matinal e a pagou em nome da NASA.

fontes.trecho: Skylab was the United States' first space station launched by NASA [...] Before re-entry, NASA ground controllers tried to adjust Skylab's orbit to minimize the risk of debris landing in populated areas, targeting the south Indian Ocean, which was partially successful. [...] British mathematician Desmond King-Hele of the Royal Aircraft Establishment (RAE) predicted in 1973 that Skylab would de-orbit and crash to Earth in 1979, sooner than NASA's forecast, because of increased solar activity. Greater-than-expected solar activity heated the outer layers of Earth's atmosphere and increased drag on Skylab. [...] wagering on the time and place of re-entry, and nightly news reports. The San Francisco Examiner offered a US$10,000 prize (equivalent to $44,000 today) for the first piece of Skylab delivered to its offices [...] and re-entry began at approximately 16:37 UTC, July 11, 1979. The station did not burn up as fast as NASA expected. Debris landed about 300 miles (480 km) east of Perth, Western Australia due to a four-percent calculation error [...] the debris landed in an almost unpopulated area [...] Stan Thornton found 24 pieces of Skylab at his home in Esperance. After obtaining his first passport, Thornton flew to San Francisco. [...] he collected the Examiner prize [...] The Shire of Esperance light-heartedly fined NASA A$400 for littering, and while the fine was indeed written off three months later, it was nonetheless eventually paid on behalf of NASA in April 2009, after Scott Barley of Highway Radio raised the funds from his morning show listeners.

gancho: O espelho do Hubble foi polido com precisão extrema, mas no formato errado: a borda ficou plana demais por cerca de 2.200 nanômetros. Como o erro era exato, deu para corrigi-lo com "óculos" instalados no espaço.
explicacao: O Hubble foi lançado em 1990 e logo se viu que tinha aberração esférica: a luz refletida na borda do espelho focava num ponto diferente da luz refletida no centro. O espelho estava entre os mais bem acabados já feitos, liso na escala de 10 nanômetros, mas sua borda estava cerca de 2.200 nanômetros mais plana do que devia. Uma comissão chefiada por Lew Allen, diretor do Jet Propulsion Laboratory, achou a origem: o corretor nulo refletivo, aparelho de teste que a fabricante Perkin-Elmer usou na etapa final do polimento, tinha sido montado com uma lente fora do lugar por 1,3 mm. Alguns testes com corretores convencionais chegaram a mostrar a aberração, mas foram descartados porque o aparelho novo era considerado mais preciso. Trocar o espelho em órbita era impossível, e trazer o telescópio de volta seria caro e demorado. Justamente por o espelho ter sido polido com tanta precisão na forma errada, deu para medir o erro e projetar componentes ópticos com exatamente o mesmo erro, no sentido oposto. Instalados por astronautas na missão de serviço STS-61, em 1993, eles funcionaram como óculos e devolveram ao telescópio a qualidade prevista no projeto.

fontes.trecho: Hubble was launched on STS-31 in 1990, but its main mirror had been ground incorrectly, resulting in spherical aberration that compromised the telescope's capabilities. The optics were corrected to their intended quality by a servicing mission, STS-61, in 1993. [...] Although it was believed to be one of the most precisely figured optical mirrors ever made, smooth to about 10 nanometers, the outer perimeter was too flat by about 2200 nanometers [...] This difference was catastrophic, introducing severe spherical aberration, a flaw in which light reflecting off the edge of a mirror focuses on a different point from the light reflecting off its center. [...] A commission headed by Lew Allen, director of the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, was established to determine how the error could have arisen. The Allen Commission found that a reflective null corrector, a testing device used to achieve a properly shaped non-spherical mirror, had been incorrectly assembled. (One lens was out of position by 1.3 mm (0.051 in).) [...] for the final manufacturing step (figuring), they switched to the custom-built reflective null corrector [...] During fabrication, a few tests using conventional null correctors correctly reported spherical aberration. But these results were dismissed, thus missing the opportunity to catch the error, because the reflective null corrector was considered more accurate. [...] it would have been impossible to replace the mirror in orbit, and too expensive and time-consuming to bring the telescope back to Earth for a refit. Instead, the fact that the mirror had been ground so precisely to the wrong shape led to the design of new optical components with exactly the same error but in the opposite sense, to be added to the telescope at the servicing mission, effectively acting as "spectacles" to correct the spherical aberration.

gancho: O Disco de Ouro das Voyager leva na capa uma amostra de urânio-238 que serve de relógio para datá-lo. E guarda as ondas cerebrais de uma mulher que pensava, entre outras coisas, em como é se apaixonar.
explicacao: As duas sondas Voyager, lançadas em 1977, carregam cópias idênticas de um disco de cobre de 30 cm banhado em ouro, com sons e imagens escolhidos para mostrar a diversidade da vida e da cultura na Terra a alguma forma de vida inteligente que os encontre. A capa traz instruções em desenho: um mapa com a posição do Sistema Solar em relação a 14 pulsares e um diagrama do átomo de hidrogênio, cuja transição entre os dois estados mais baixos serve de unidade de tempo. Nessa unidade, escrita em binário, a capa informa que o disco leva 3,6 segundos para dar uma volta. Sobre a capa de alumínio foi depositada uma amostra ultrapura de urânio-238, cuja meia-vida é de 4,468 bilhões de anos: pela proporção entre o urânio que restou e outros elementos, uma civilização poderia calcular a idade do disco. Entre peças de Bach, Mozart, Beethoven, Chuck Berry e de muitas culturas, há uma gravação de uma hora das ondas cerebrais de Ann Druyan, diretora criativa do projeto, comprimida num minuto de áudio. Enquanto era gravada, ela pensou na história da Terra, nas civilizações e seus problemas e em como é se apaixonar.

fontes.trecho: The Voyager Golden Records are two identical phonograph records, with one copy aboard each of the two Voyager spacecraft launched in 1977. The records contain sounds and data to reconstruct raster scan images selected to portray the diversity of life and culture on Earth, and are intended for any intelligent extraterrestrial life form who may find them. [...] featuring works by composers such as J. S. Bach, Mozart, Beethoven and Stravinsky. The disc also includes music by Guan Pinghu, Blind Willie Johnson, Louis Armstrong, Chuck Berry [...] Ann Druyan as creative director [...] The Golden Record also carries an hour-long recording of the brainwaves of Ann Druyan, compressed into a minute of audio. During the recording of the brainwaves, Druyan thought of many topics, including Earth's history, civilizations and the problems they face, and what it was like to fall in love. [...] The record is a copper disk 12 inches (30 cm) in diameter plated first with nickel and then gold. The record's cover is aluminum and electroplated upon it is an ultra-pure sample of the isotope uranium-238. Uranium-238 has a half-life of 4.468 billion years. It is possible (e.g., via mass spectrometry) that a civilization that encounters the record will be able to use the ratio of remaining uranium to the other elements to determine the age of the record. [...] Written around it in binary notation is the correct time of one rotation of the record, 3.6 seconds, expressed in time units of 0.70 billionths of a second, the time period associated with the radiation emitted or absorbed by a fundamental transition of the hydrogen atom. [...] It shows the location of the Solar System with respect to 14 pulsars, whose precise periods are given. The drawing containing two circles in the lower right-hand corner is a drawing of the hydrogen atom in its two lowest states, with a connecting line and digit 1 to indicate that the time interval associated with the transition from one state to the other is to be used as the fundamental time scale

gancho: O helicóptero Ingenuity, que voou em Marte, levava um pedacinho do tecido da asa do avião dos irmãos Wright, de 1903. E a área de onde decolou ganhou da aviação civil um código de aeroporto: JZRO.
explicacao: O Ingenuity fez seu primeiro voo em 19 de abril de 2021, o primeiro voo motorizado e controlado de uma aeronave fora da Terra. A NASA e o JPL o chamaram de seu "momento irmãos Wright", em referência ao primeiro voo bem-sucedido de um avião motorizado. Para marcar a ligação, um pedacinho do tecido da asa do Wright Flyer, de 1903, foi preso a um cabo sob o painel solar do helicóptero. Não era a primeira vez: em 1969, Neil Armstrong levou à Lua, no módulo lunar Eagle, um artefato semelhante do mesmo avião. A área de decolagem e pouso em Marte foi batizada de Campo Irmãos Wright, e a OACI, a agência da ONU para aviação civil, deu a ela o código JZRO, de cratera Jezero. Voar ali é difícil: o ar de Marte tem cerca de 1/100 da densidade do ar terrestre ao nível do mar, o mesmo que a 27 mil metros de altitude, onde nenhum helicóptero jamais chegou. Por isso, as pás precisavam girar entre 2.400 e 2.900 rotações por minuto, cerca de dez vezes mais rápido do que na Terra. Planejado para apenas cinco voos, o Ingenuity fez 72 em quase três anos.

fontes.trecho: Ingenuity made its first flight on 19 April 2021, demonstrating that flight is possible in the extremely thin atmosphere of Mars, and became the first aircraft to conduct a powered and controlled extraterrestrial flight. [...] Originally intended to make only five flights, Ingenuity completed 72 flights over the course of nearly three years. [...] The planet's atmospheric density is about 1⁄100 that of Earth's at sea level, or about the same as at 27,000 m (87,000 ft), an altitude never reached by existing helicopters. [...] To keep Ingenuity aloft, its specially shaped blades of enlarged size must rotate between 2400 and 2900 rpm, or about 10 times faster than what is needed on Earth. [...] NASA and JPL officials described the first Mars Ingenuity helicopter flight as their "Wright Brothers moment", by analogy to the first successful powered airplane flight on Earth. A small piece of the wing cloth from the Wright brothers' 1903 Wright Flyer is attached to a cable underneath Ingenuity's solar panel. In 1969, Apollo 11's Neil Armstrong carried a similar Wright Flyer artifact to the Moon in the Lunar Module Eagle. NASA named Ingenuity's first take-off and landing airstrip Wright Brothers Field, which the UN agency ICAO gave an airport code of JZRO for Jezero Crater

gancho: É falsa a história da NASA gastando milhões numa caneta espacial enquanto os russos usavam lápis. A caneta foi criada com dinheiro privado, e os soviéticos acabaram comprando o mesmo modelo.
explicacao: A lenda diz que a NASA gastou uma fortuna para criar uma caneta que escrevesse sem gravidade, enquanto os soviéticos resolveram tudo com lápis. Na verdade, a NASA também usava lápis: há um pedido de lapiseiras de 1965. Só que o lápis é um problema no espaço: pontas quebradas e pó de grafite flutuando ameaçam a eletrônica, a madeira pega fogo, e anotações que borram ou se apagam não servem como registro. A Space Pen foi desenvolvida com capital privado: a tinta especial custou a Paul Fisher cerca de 1 milhão de dólares, e a NASA nunca encomendou a caneta nem a financiou. Fisher a inventou por conta própria e, em 1965, pediu à agência que a testasse. Depois de muitos testes, ela foi adotada nas missões Apollo, e em 1967 noticiou-se que a NASA comprou cerca de 400 unidades a 2,95 dólares cada. O truque está no cartucho selado, em que nitrogênio comprimido empurra a tinta, o que permite escrever em qualquer ângulo. Os cosmonautas soviéticos usavam lápis e lápis dermatográficos em pranchetas de plástico até 1969, quando também adotaram a caneta, com uma compra de 100 unidades.

fontes.trecho: An urban legend states that NASA spent a large amount of money to develop a pen that would write in space (the result purportedly being the Fisher Space Pen), while the Soviets just used pencils. [...] However, the claim that NASA spent millions on the Space Pen is incorrect, as the Fisher pen was developed using private capital, not government funding. The development of the thixotropic ink cost Paul Fisher around $1 million [...] NASA programs previously used pencils (as demonstrated by an order in 1965 for mechanical pencils) but because of the substantial dangers that broken pencil tips and graphite dust pose to electronics in zero gravity, the flammable nature of wood present in pencils, and the inadequate quality documentation produced by non-permanent or smeared recordkeeping, a better solution was needed. Soviet cosmonauts used pencils, and grease pencils on plastic slates until also adopting a space pen in 1969 with a purchase of 100 units for use on all future missions. NASA never approached Paul Fisher to develop a pen, nor did Fisher receive any government funding for the pen's development. Fisher invented it independently and then, in 1965, asked NASA to try it. After extensive testing, NASA decided to use the pens in future Apollo missions. Subsequently, in 1967 it was reported that NASA purchased approximately 400 pens for $2.95 apiece [...] The ink is forced out by compressed nitrogen at a pressure of nearly 310 kPa [...] The pen can write without the help of gravity, at any angle.

gancho: Em 1957, o primeiro foguete dos EUA a tentar pôr um satélite em órbita subiu cerca de um metro e explodiu: virou o "Flopnik". O satélite do mesmo programa lançado em 1958 é o objeto artificial mais antigo em órbita.
explicacao: Depois dos Sputnik 1 e 2, os Estados Unidos tentaram responder com o Vanguard TV-3, em 6 de dezembro de 1957. Uns dois segundos após a decolagem, o foguete perdeu empuxo, voltou a cair sobre a plataforma e explodiu. O pequeno satélite foi arremessado e parou no chão ali perto, ainda emitindo seu sinal de rádio. Os jornais brincaram com o nome do Sputnik e falaram em "Flopnik", "Kaputnik" e "Stayputnik", a Bolsa de Nova York suspendeu por um tempo a negociação das ações da principal fabricante, e um delegado soviético na ONU perguntou se os EUA tinham interesse em receber ajuda reservada a países subdesenvolvidos. Em março de 1958, o Vanguard 1 enfim chegou à órbita. Era uma esfera de alumínio de 1,46 kg, que Khrushchev chamou de "satélite toranja", e o primeiro satélite com energia solar: seu transmissor ligado a células solares funcionou por mais de seis anos. O contato acabou em 1964, mas ele continua lá, junto com o estágio superior do foguete: são os objetos artificiais mais antigos ainda em órbita. A previsão inicial era de 2 mil anos em órbita; a pressão da radiação solar e o arrasto da atmosfera em períodos de Sol ativo reduziram a estimativa para cerca de 240 anos.

fontes.trecho: Vanguard TV-3 (also called Vanguard Test Vehicle-Three), was the first attempt of the United States to launch a satellite into orbit around the Earth, after the successful Soviet launches of Sputnik 1 and Sputnik 2. [...] At its launch attempt on 6 December 1957, at Cape Canaveral Air Force Station, the booster ignited and began to rise, but about two seconds after liftoff, after rising about 1.2 m (four feet), the rocket lost thrust and fell back to the launch pad. As it settled, the fuel tanks ruptured and exploded, destroying the rocket and severely damaging the launch pad. The Vanguard 1A satellite was thrown clear and landed on the ground a short distance away with its transmitters still sending out a beacon signal. [...] After the launch failure, trading in the stock of the Martin Company, the prime contractor for the project, was temporarily suspended by the New York Stock Exchange. Newspapers in the United States published prominent headlines and articles describing the failure with plays on the name of the Russian satellite, Sputnik, such as "Flopnik", "Kaputnik", "Oopsnik", "Dudnick"  and "Stayputnik". [...] A few days after the incident, a Soviet delegate to the United Nations inquired whether the United States was interested in receiving aid earmarked for "undeveloped countries".

It was launched 17 March 1958. Vanguard 1 was the first satellite to have solar electric power. Although communications with the satellite were lost in 1964, it remains the oldest artificial object still in orbit, together with the upper stage of its launch vehicle. [...] was described by the Soviet Premier, Nikita Khrushchev, as "the grapefruit satellite". [...] The spacecraft is a 1.46 kg (3.2 lb) aluminum sphere [...] Original estimates had the orbit lasting for 2,000 years, but it was discovered that solar radiation pressure and atmospheric drag during high levels of solar activity produced significant perturbations in the perigee height of the satellite, which caused a significant decrease in its expected lifetime to about 240 years. [...] The solar-cell-powered transmitter operated for more than six years.

gancho: Em 2003, um motor do foguete brasileiro VLS-1 teve uma ignição não planejada na plataforma de Alcântara e matou 21 pessoas. Foi o maior acidente da história do programa espacial brasileiro.
explicacao: O VLS-1 deveria pôr dois satélites em órbita. As tentativas anteriores, em 1997 e 1999, tinham falhado em voo. Na terceira, em 22 de agosto de 2003, dias antes da data marcada para o lançamento, um dos motores do primeiro estágio pegou fogo enquanto havia gente trabalhando nos cinco andares da torre móvel de integração. Em cerca de oito segundos, a torre foi envolvida por fumaça e gases a até 3.000 °C, e ela desabou cinco minutos depois. Segundo as normas de segurança, só seis pessoas poderiam estar no local, mas havia muito mais. Contra o regulamento, o sistema de ignição tinha sido instalado em dois motores na manhã do acidente, embora o cronograma o previsse para o dia seguinte. O relatório final, apresentado em 2004 com a participação de especialistas russos, apontou a descarga eletrostática como a hipótese mais forte e não identificou nenhum erro ou violação que tivesse causado o acidente diretamente. Mas citou a verba limitada e a falta de pessoal como fatores que contribuíram. O acidente atrasou muito o programa espacial brasileiro, e o projeto do VLS-1 foi encerrado pela Agência Espacial Brasileira em 2016.

fontes.trecho: was an accident during the Brazilian Space Agency's third attempt to launch the VLS-1 rocket, which was intended to launch two satellites into orbit. The rocket ignited on its launch pad at the Alcântara Launch Center, killing 21 people. It is officially the fourth deadliest space exploration related disaster in history. [...] The rocket, proposed in 1979 had two launch attempts until the accident: one in 1997, which ended up in the Atlantic Ocean due to the failure of one of the first stage engines to start and another in 1999, destroyed remotely due to a flame penetrating the top of the second stage block after takeoff. [...] The accident occurred three days before the scheduled launch date, at 1:26:06 pm (Brasília time) on August 22, 2003, between frames 26 and 27 recorded by the Closed Circuit TV of the Mobile Integration Tower, with professionals spread across the five floors of the tower. [...] An unplanned ignition, which began in a first-stage engine that caught fire after ignition, destroyed the launch vehicle while it was on the CLA launch pad. [...] It took about eight seconds before the tower was enveloped by smoke and gases heated up to 3,000 °C. The mobile tower stood upright for five minutes, collapsing at 1:31. [...] However, the number of people at the base was well above safety standards, which allowed for only six people to be present. The accident significantly delayed the Brazilian space program. It was later revealed that, contrary to the regulations, on the morning of the 22nd, the ignition system was installed in only two engines, even though the schedule indicated that this should have been done on the 23rd [...] The report was presented by the ministers of Defense and Science on 16 March 2004. The conclusion of both the Brazilian and Russian investigators was that the cause of the accident was due to the unplanned start of the A-booster. [...] The electrostatic discharge hypothesis was found to be superior [...] Overall, the report did not identify any "active failure" (error or violation) that caused the accident. However, it cited limited funding and a shortage of staff as contributing factors to the incident.
The 2003 Alcântara VLS accident caused a considerable setback to the Brazilian space program. [...] The project was terminated by Brazilian Space Agency in 2016.

fontes.titulo: Base de Alcântara: 20 anos do maior acidente da história do Programa Espacial Brasileiro (Olhar Digital)
fontes.trecho: o Veículo Lançador de Satélites VLS-1 V03, um foguete de 21 metros de altura, explodiu em uma ignição prematura na Torre Móvel de Integração (TMI) por volta das 13h30 (hora local), matando 21 técnicos, engenheiros e cientistas – se tornando o maior acidente da história do Programa Espacial Brasileiro.

gancho: A Apollo 12 foi atingida por dois raios logo depois de decolar, em 1969, e o painel se encheu de alertas. Um controlador lembrou de um teste antigo e sugeriu uma chave obscura: "SCE to Aux". Funcionou.
explicacao: O lançamento foi num dia chuvoso, sob céu totalmente encoberto. Aos 36,5 segundos de voo, um raio, desencadeado pelo próprio foguete, atingiu o Saturno V. A descarga desligou as três células de combustível, e a nave ficou dependendo de baterias que não davam conta da demanda. Um segundo raio, aos 52 segundos, derrubou o indicador de atitude. Os dados que chegavam a Houston viraram uma confusão, e os astronautas viam o painel cheio de luzes de alerta sem saber o que estava errado. O foguete seguia normalmente, porque seu sistema de guiagem funcionava de forma independente da nave. No controle da missão, John Aaron reconheceu o padrão de falha de um teste anterior e pediu para passar o condicionador de sinais, o SCE, para a alimentação reserva. Nem o diretor de voo nem o comandante Pete Conrad sabiam que chave era essa; Alan Bean, o engenheiro da nave, sabia onde ficava e a acionou. A telemetria voltou e mostrou que não havia pane grave. Sobrou um temor, que não foi contado à tripulação: o raio podia ter danificado os parafusos explosivos que abriam o compartimento dos paraquedas. Como abortar não mudaria esse risco, a missão seguiu. No fim, os paraquedas abriram normalmente.

fontes.trecho: It was launched on November 14, 1969, by NASA from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida [...] Commander Charles "Pete" Conrad and Lunar Module Pilot Alan L. Bean [...] Shortly after being launched on a rainy day at Kennedy Space Center, Apollo 12 was twice struck by lightning, causing instrumentation problems but little damage. [...] There were completely overcast rainy skies [...] Lightning struck the Saturn V 36.5 seconds after lift-off, triggered by the vehicle itself. The static discharge caused a voltage transient that knocked all three fuel cells offline, meaning the spacecraft was being powered entirely from its batteries, which could not supply enough current to meet demand. A second strike at 52 seconds knocked out the "8-ball" attitude indicator. The telemetry stream at Mission Control was garbled, but the Saturn V continued to fly normally; the strikes had not affected the Saturn V instrument unit guidance system, which functioned independently from the CSM. The astronauts unexpectedly had a board red with caution and warning lights, but could not tell exactly what was wrong. The Electrical, Environmental and Consumables Manager (EECOM) in Mission Control, John Aaron, remembered the telemetry failure pattern from an earlier test when a power loss caused a malfunction in the CSM signal conditioning electronics (SCE) [...] Aaron made a call, "Flight, EECOM. Try SCE to Aux", to switch the SCE to a backup power supply. The switch was fairly obscure, and neither Flight Director Gerald Griffin, CAPCOM Gerald P. Carr, nor Conrad knew what it was; Bean, who as LMP was the spacecraft's engineer, knew where to find it and threw the switch, after which the telemetry came back online, revealing no significant malfunctions. [...] Initially, it was feared that the lightning strike could have damaged the explosive bolts that opened the Command Module's parachute compartment. The decision was made not to share this with the astronauts and to continue with the flight plan, since they would die if the parachutes failed to deploy, whether following an Earth-orbit abort or upon a return from the Moon, so nothing was to be gained by aborting. The parachutes deployed and functioned normally at the end of the mission.

gancho: Os trajes que os astronautas da Apollo usaram na Lua foram feitos por uma divisão da Playtex, fabricante de sutiãs. Nas costuras, as costureiras tinham uma tolerância de menos de 1/64 de polegada (cerca de 0,4 mm).
explicacao: A International Latex Corporation, fundada em 1932 e mais tarde conhecida como Playtex, ficou famosa pelas roupas íntimas femininas. Uma divisão dela, sediada em Dover, nos EUA, fazia capacetes e trajes pressurizados para grandes altitudes. Em 1965, essa divisão ganhou o contrato do traje lunar da Apollo graças ao seu jeito de fazer juntas flexíveis em trajes cheios de ar. Segundo uma resenha do livro Spacesuit: Fashioning Apollo, de Nicholas de Monchaux, citada pela revista Smithsonian, a equipe, liderada por um mecânico de automóveis e um ex-técnico de televisão, entrou na concorrência por conta própria e passou seis semanas trabalhando dia e noite, até criar um traje que superou com folga os dois concorrentes convidados. Parte das costureiras veio da divisão Playtex; outras, de fábricas de roupas e malas da região. Elas tiveram de aprender a trabalhar devagar, com tecidos novos e com regras de engenharia da NASA muito mais rígidas que as da confecção comum: o desvio tolerado nas costuras era menor que 1/64 de polegada. Cada traje era feito sob medida, e para cada um dos 12 voos tripulados a empresa produziu 15. Em 2012, segundo a Smithsonian, mais de 300 trajes espaciais, entre eles o de Neil Armstrong, estavam no acervo do Museu Nacional do Ar e do Espaço, envoltos em musselina para absorver o ácido clorídrico que liberam.

fontes.trecho: ILC outfitted every United States astronaut in the Apollo program, including the twelve that walked on the Moon. [...] ILC Dover initially formed as a branch of the International Latex Corporation,  the company founded in 1932 by Abram Spanel and later known as Playtex best known for manufacture of women's undergarments. [...] Located at that time in Dover, Delaware, ILC's earliest work was on high-altitude pressure helmets and high-altitude pressure suits for the U.S Navy and Air Force. In 1965, ILC (then known as the Government and Industrial Division of the International Latex Corporation) was awarded the prime contract for the Apollo Lunar Space Suit, based on its unique approach to designing flexible joints in air filled suits. [...] Apollo spacesuits were custom-made for each of the astronauts in the program, and for each of the 12 crewed flights carried out, ILC produced 15 suits.

Some of the women had been recruited from the Playtex division of ILC, while other came from nearby clothing and luggage manufacturers. [...] However to succeed at ILC, the women had to be willing to learn new sewing techniques, perform their tasks at a slow pace, work with novel textiles, and perform to exacting standards. [...] The production line at ILC followed NASA-mandated engineering guidelines that were significantly stricter than typical clothing manufacturing processes. Tolerance for variation in the stitches were less than 1/64 of an inch from the seam.

fontes.titulo: What Did Playtex Have to Do With Neil Armstrong? (Smithsonian Magazine)
fontes.trecho: August 27, 2012 [...] From the book Spacesuit: Fashioning Apollo, by Nicholas de Monchaux [...] Over 300 spacesuits, including the one Armstrong wore on the Apollo 11 mission, are in the Smithsonian collection at the National Air and Space Museum. They are lovingly cared for, conserved and covered in muslin (to absorb the hydrochloric acid the suits emit) [...] was a product of the industrial division of the women’s bra manufacturer Playtex. The L.A. Review of Books, in reviewing Spacesuit: Fashioning Apollo, described how [...] ILC’s team , a motley group of seamstresses and engineers, led by a car mechanic and a former television repairman, manages to convince NASA to let them enter their “test suit” in a closed, invitation-only competitive bid at their own expense. They spend six weeks working around the clock—at times breaking into their own offices to work 24-hour shifts—to arrive at a suit solution that starkly outperforms the two invited competitors.

gancho: Por anos, as sondas Pioneer 10 e 11 frearam um pouco mais do que a gravidade explicava, e houve quem propusesse mudar as leis da física. A culpa era do calor da própria nave, irradiado mais para um lado.
explicacao: As duas sondas, lançadas em 1972 e 1973, estão saindo do Sistema Solar, freadas aos poucos pela gravidade do Sol. Depois de passarem de cerca de 20 unidades astronômicas, os dados de navegação mostraram que elas freavam um pouquinho além do esperado, o equivalente a perder 1 km/h de velocidade a cada dez anos. A diferença foi notada já em 1980, mas só passou a ser investigada a sério em 1994. As propostas iam de causas banais, como erro de medida, vazamento de gás ou calor irradiado de forma desigual, até "física nova", com mudanças na gravitação, como a hipótese MOND. Uma explicação gravitacional esbarrava num problema: o efeito não aparecia nas órbitas dos planetas externos. Entre 1998 e 2012, uma explicação se firmou. Cada sonda é alimentada por um gerador a radioisótopo e, cercada de vácuo, só consegue perder calor por radiação. Se o formato da nave faz o calor sair mais para um lado, o recuo dos fótons térmicos empurra a sonda de leve no sentido oposto. Em 2012, vários grupos refizeram com cuidado as contas dessas forças térmicas e mostraram que elas explicam a anomalia inteira: a causa é banal e não exige mudar as leis da física.

fontes.trecho: The Pioneer anomaly, or Pioneer effect, was the observed deviation from predicted accelerations of the Pioneer 10 and Pioneer 11 spacecraft after they passed about 20 astronomical units [...] has been subsequently explained by anisotropic radiation pressure caused by the spacecraft's heat loss. Both Pioneer spacecraft are escaping the Solar System but are slowing under the influence of the Sun's gravity. Upon very close examination of navigational data, the spacecraft were found to be slowing slightly more than expected. [...] which is equivalent to a reduction of the outbound velocity by 1 km/h over a period of ten years. The two spacecraft were launched in 1972 and 1973. The anomalous acceleration was first noticed as early as 1980 but not seriously investigated until 1994. [...] Over the period from 1998 to 2012, one particular explanation became accepted. The spacecraft, which are surrounded by an ultra-high vacuum and are each powered by a radioisotope thermoelectric generator (RTG), can shed heat only via thermal radiation. If, due to the design of the spacecraft, more heat is emitted in a particular direction by what is known as a radiative anisotropy, then the spacecraft would accelerate slightly in the direction opposite of the excess emitted radiation due to the recoil of thermal photons. [...] By 2012, several papers by different groups, all reanalyzing the thermal radiation pressure forces inherent in the spacecraft, showed that a careful accounting of this explains the entire anomaly; thus the cause is mundane and does not point to any new phenomenon or need to update the laws of physics. [...] other proposed explanations fell into two classes –"mundane causes" or "new physics". Mundane causes include conventional effects that were overlooked or mis-modeled in the initial analysis, such as measurement error, thrust from gas leakage, or uneven heat radiation. The "new physics" explanations proposed revision of our understanding of gravitational physics. [...] However, this acceleration does not show up in the orbits of the outer planets [...] MOND hypothesis proposed that the force of gravity deviates from the traditional Newtonian value

gancho: O engenheiro por trás do Sputnik e do voo de Gagarin era apresentado só como "projetista-chefe": nem alguns cosmonautas sabiam seu nome. Anos antes, ele perdera a maioria dos dentes num campo do Gulag.
explicacao: Sergei Korolev dirigiu o desenvolvimento do R-7, o primeiro míssil balístico intercontinental do mundo, e versões dele lançaram o Sputnik 1, a cadela Laika e o voo de Iuri Gagarin. Antes disso, em 1938, durante o Grande Expurgo de Stálin, ele foi preso com acusações depois reconhecidas como falsas. Chegou a ser condenado à morte, pena trocada por trabalhos forçados, e passou quase seis anos entre prisões e campos. Em Kolyma, no extremo leste da Sibéria, trabalhou meses numa mina de ouro e perdeu a maior parte dos dentes por escorbuto. Depois, com a ajuda do antigo mentor Andrei Tupolev, foi transferido para uma prisão onde cientistas e engenheiros trabalhavam em projetos do Estado. Na era espacial, os nomes dos chefes do programa soviético viraram segredo: o relatório sobre o Sputnik 1 saiu anônimo no Pravda, e Korolev escrevia artigos como "Professor K. Sergeyev". Em público, era só o "projetista-chefe", em parte para protegê-lo de atentados durante a Guerra Fria. Sua identidade só foi revelada depois que ele morreu, em 1966. Segundo uma das versões sobre a morte, durante uma cirurgia os médicos não conseguiram intubá-lo porque as mandíbulas dele, feridas no Gulag, não tinham se recuperado direito.

fontes.trecho: Korolev directed development of the R-7 rocket, the world's first intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM) and was a leader in the Soviet space programme which used modified versions of the R-7 for several notable achievements. Under his leadership, the Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1, the first artificial satellite; Laika, the first animal to orbit Earth; [...] He also directed the missions that carried Yuri Gagarin into space aboard Vostok 1 [...] In 1938 he was arrested during the Great Purge on charges later shown to be false and spent nearly six years in prison and labour camps, including several months in Kolyma. Prior to his imprisonment, Korolev had been initially condemned to be executed under Joseph Stalin's orders among 74 military specialists and engineers before his sentence was commuted to hard prison labour. [...] During his lifetime, Korolev was publicly identified only as glavny konstruktor (главный конструктор; lit. 'chief designer'), partly to protect him from possible assassination attempts during the Cold War. Even some cosmonauts who worked with him did not know his name. His identity was publicly disclosed only after his death in 1966 [...] Korolev was on his way from prison to a Gulag forced labour camp in Kolyma in the far east of Siberia, where he spent several months in a gold mine before word reached him of his retrial. [...] Korolev sustained injuries, including possibly a heart attack and lost most of his teeth from scurvy before being returned to Moscow in late 1939. [...] However, due to the intervention by his old mentor, Andrei Tupolev, he was relocated to a prison for scientists and engineers in September 1940. [...] For security reasons, the names of chief individuals in the Soviet space program became a secret. They were allowed to prepare a report detailing the design and construction of Sputnik 1, however, which was published anonymously by Pravda on 9 October. Korolev also began writing other articles under the pseudonym "Professor K. Sergeyev". [...] Doctors tried to provide intubation to allow him to breathe freely, but his jaws, injured during his time in a Gulag, had not healed properly and impeded the installation of the breathing tube.

gancho: Em 1969, o módulo lunar da Apollo 10 chegou a 14,4 km da Lua sem poder pousar: tinha só metade do combustível para voltar. Sua parte de cima foi mandada para uma órbita em torno do Sol, e talvez tenha sido reencontrada.
explicacao: A NASA descreveu a Apollo 10 como o "ensaio geral" do primeiro pouso, feito dois meses depois pela Apollo 11. O módulo lunar, chamado Snoopy, levou Stafford e Cernan até 14,4 km da superfície. Pousar estava fora de questão: segundo um dirigente da NASA, aquele módulo era um modelo antigo, pesado demais para decolar da Lua e voltar à nave-mãe. Além disso, o estágio de subida levava só o combustível que sobraria depois de uma decolagem real, cerca de metade do necessário. Cernan contou depois que havia quem pensasse: não deem a esses caras a chance de pousar, porque eles podem pousar. Depois do reencontro com o módulo de comando, chamado Charlie Brown, o combustível restante do estágio de subida do Snoopy foi queimado para mandá-lo a uma órbita em torno do Sol, destino único entre os módulos lunares da Apollo. A órbita deixou de ser acompanhada depois de 1969. Em 2011, astrônomos amadores britânicos começaram a procurá-lo e, em 2019, o grupo anunciou uma possível redescoberta: o pequeno asteroide 2018 AV2 seria o Snoopy, com "98%" de certeza, segundo a equipe do astrônomo amador Nick Howes, que liderava a busca. Até onde se sabe, é a única nave que já levou tripulantes e que segue vagando pelo espaço, vazia.

fontes.trecho: NASA, the mission's operator, described it as a "dress rehearsal" for the first Moon landing (Apollo 11, two months later). [...] The mission's call signs were the names of the Peanuts characters Charlie Brown for the CSM and Snoopy for the LM [...] The ascent stage was loaded with the amount of fuel and oxidizer it would have had remaining if it had lifted off from the surface and reached the altitude at which the Apollo 10 ascent stage fired; this was only about half the total amount required for lift off and rendezvous with the CSM. [...] Nelson quoted Cernan as saying "A lot of people thought about the kind of people we were: 'Don't give those guys an opportunity to land, 'cause they might!' So the ascent module, the part we lifted off the lunar surface with, was short-fueled. The fuel tanks weren't full. So had we literally tried to land on the Moon, we couldn't have gotten off." Mueller, NASA's Associate Administrator for Manned Space Flight, stated, [...] It was an early design that was too heavy for a lunar landing, or, to be more precise, too heavy to be able to complete the ascent back to the command module. [...] when the craft came within 14.4 kilometers (7.8 nautical miles; 9 miles) of the Moon, its closest approach. [...] The rest of the LM's ascent-stage engine fuel was burned to send it on a trajectory past the Moon and into a heliocentric orbit. It was the only Apollo LM to meet this fate. [...] Snoopy's ascent stage orbit was not tracked after 1969, and its whereabouts were unknown. In 2011, a group of amateur astronomers in the UK started a project to search for it. In June 2019, the Royal Astronomical Society announced a possible rediscovery of Snoopy, determining that small Earth-crossing asteroid 2018 AV2 is likely to be the spacecraft with "98%" certainty. It is the only once-crewed spacecraft known to still be in outer space without a crew.

fontes.titulo: Apollo 10's Snoopy Lunar Lander May Have Been Found in Space (Universe Today)
fontes.trecho: Then in 2011, a group of amateur astronomers in the UK began looking for Snoopy. At the time, Universe Today covered the effort by amateur astronomer Nick Howes to search for Snoopy. [...] Now, 8 years later, Howes thinks they've found Snoopy at long last. [...] A report on Sky News says that the team is almost certain they've found it. Or 98% certain, anyway. [...] Howes stressed that some agency will have to get a better look at it before they can confirm that the object is Snoopy.

gancho: Em 2022, a NASA jogou uma sonda contra uma pequena lua de asteroide para ver se dava para desviá-la. A meta mínima era mudar a órbita em 73 segundos. Mudou em 32 minutos, e o empurrão veio mais dos detritos.
explicacao: A missão DART, sigla em inglês para Teste de Redirecionamento de Asteroide Duplo, mirou Dimorphos, uma lua que gira em volta do asteroide Didymos. A sonda se chocou contra ela em 26 de setembro de 2022, a cerca de 23.000 km/h, a uns 11 milhões de quilômetros da Terra. Antes da batida, Dimorphos dava uma volta em Didymos em 11 horas e 55 minutos; depois, em 11 horas e 23 minutos, segundo a NASA, com margem de uns 2 minutos. O critério de sucesso fixado antes era bem mais modesto: 73 segundos. O resultado passou dessa marca mais de 25 vezes. A explicação está no material arrancado da superfície. Os detritos lançados ao espaço funcionaram como um recuo, e esse recuo foi bem maior do que o empurrão da própria sonda. Para a NASA, foi a primeira vez que a humanidade mudou de propósito o movimento de um corpo celeste e a primeira demonstração em escala real de uma técnica para desviar asteroides. Estudos posteriores ainda concluíram que a batida alterou levemente a órbita do par de asteroides em volta do Sol.

fontes.titulo: NASA Confirms DART Mission Impact Changed Asteroid's Motion in Space
fontes.trecho: This marks humanity's first time purposely changing the motion of a celestial object and the first full-scale demonstration of asteroid deflection technology. [...] the investigation team has confirmed the spacecraft's impact altered Dimorphos' orbit around Didymos by 32 minutes, shortening the 11 hour and 55-minute orbit to 11 hours and 23 minutes. This measurement has a margin of uncertainty of approximately plus or minus 2 minutes. Before its encounter, NASA had defined a minimum successful orbit period change of Dimorphos as change of 73 seconds or more. This early data show DART surpassed this minimum benchmark by more than 25 times.

the DART spacecraft collided with Dimorphos at 14,000 mph (23,000 km/h) on 26 September 2022 about 6.8 million miles (10.9 million kilometers) from Earth. The collision shortened Dimorphos's orbit around Didymos by 32 minutes, greatly in excess of the pre-defined success threshold of 73 seconds. Deflection resulted from the ejection of debris which caused a recoil that was substantially larger than the impact itself. [...] Scientists later determined that the impact also slightly changed the orbit of the asteroid pair around the Sun

gancho: Em 1908, uma explosão na Sibéria derrubou milhões de árvores numa área de mais de 2.150 km². Quem foi ao local esperava uma cratera e não achou nenhuma: no centro, as árvores continuavam de pé, sem galhos.
explicacao: O evento de Tunguska, em 30 de junho de 1908, devastou uma região remota da taiga siberiana. A onda de choque jogou testemunhas no chão, matou pelo menos três pessoas e quebrou janelas num raio de 200 km. A primeira expedição científica, liderada por Leonid Kulik, foi organizada em 1921, mas ele só achou o epicentro em 1927. A equipe esperava uma cratera de impacto e se surpreendeu: não havia nenhuma. Havia, sim, uma zona de uns 8 km em que as árvores estavam chamuscadas e sem galhos, mas em pé. Em volta, os troncos caídos formavam um padrão radial, como as asas de uma borboleta, e esse desenho indicava uma origem aérea. O padrão se explica pela geometria da explosão: logo abaixo dela, a onda de choque desceu quase na vertical, arrancou os galhos e deixou os troncos em pé; mais longe, chegou quase na horizontal e deitou as árvores. O consenso científico atribui o evento a um meteoroide que explodiu na atmosfera. A hipótese preferida é a de um corpo de 50 a 60 metros (se asteroide ou cometa, ainda se discute) que explodiu entre 5 e 10 km de altitude. Nas noites seguintes, o céu ficou tão claro numa área de uns 12 milhões de km², no oeste da Eurásia, que deu para ler jornal à meia-noite sem luz artificial.

fontes.trecho: The Tunguska event was a large explosion that occurred on the morning of 30 June [O.S. 17 June] 1908 [...] The cataclysm occurred in a remote and sparsely populated region of the taiga [...] devastated the taiga, flattening several million trees over an area of more than 2,150 km2 (830 sq mi), while decimating numerous reindeer and dogs belonging to the Evenks. Under the effect of the shock wave, the trees were felled in a radial pattern forming the characteristic shape of two "butterfly wings" around the central area. At the epicenter itself, the blast stripped the trees of their branches but left them standing [...] The shock wave knocked several witnesses to the ground, killed at least three people as well as numerous animals, and shattered windows within a 200 km (120 mi) radius. [...] researchers favor the hypothesis of a 50–60 m (160–200 ft) diameter meteoroid moving at high speed from the south-east. The object would have exploded between 5–10 km (3.1–6.2 mi) in altitude [...] it became possible to read a newspaper or photograph monuments around midnight without artificial lighting. [...] From 30 June to 3 July, intense bright nights were observed across western Eurasia over an area of about 12,000,000 km2 (4,600,000 sq mi). [...] it was not until 1921 that a first scientific expedition was organized under the direction of Leonid Kulik, who discovered the site of the epicenter only in 1927. Kulik and his successors' research revealed that the explosion devastated nearly 2,150 km2 (830 sq mi) of forest in a radial pattern which implied an aerial origin. The scientific consensus thus attributes this event to a meteor air burst, the atmospheric explosion of a celestial [...] Kulik led a scientific expedition to the Tunguska blast site in 1927. He hired local Evenki hunters to guide his team to the centre of the blast area, where they expected to find an impact crater. To their surprise, there was no crater at ground zero. Instead, they found a zone, roughly 8 km (5.0 mi) across, where the trees were scorched and devoid of branches, but still standing upright [...] The trees directly below the explosion are stripped as the blast wave moves vertically downward, but remain standing upright, while trees farther away are knocked over because the blast wave is travelling closer to horizontal when it reaches them.

gancho: Em 2013, enquanto o mundo esperava a passagem prevista de um asteroide, outro, que ninguém viu chegar, vindo do lado do Sol, explodiu sobre a Rússia. A maioria dos 1.491 feridos foi atingida por vidro quebrado.
explicacao: O meteoro de Chelyabinsk, uma rocha de uns 17 a 20 metros segundo a NASA, entrou na atmosfera em 15 de fevereiro de 2013 e por um instante brilhou mais que o Sol. Ele não foi detectado antes, em parte porque chegou do lado do céu onde está o Sol. No mesmo dia, cerca de 16 horas depois, passaria pela Terra um asteroide maior, o 367943 Duende, previsto havia muito tempo; as órbitas mostraram que os dois não tinham relação. Nenhum pedaço do meteoro atingiu alguém. Os ferimentos vieram de efeitos indiretos, sobretudo de vidraças estouradas pela onda de choque, que chegou minutos depois do clarão; cerca de 7.200 prédios foram danificados. Numa escola de Chelyabinsk, a professora Yulia Karbysheva, sem saber o que era a luz, mandou os 44 alunos se afastarem das janelas e se abrigarem sob as carteiras. Ela ficou de pé e teve um tendão cortado pelo vidro; nenhum aluno se feriu. O clarão também causou dor nos olhos e queimaduras parecidas com as de sol.

fontes.trecho: was a superbolide that entered Earth's atmosphere over the southern Ural region in Russia on 15 February 2013 [...] The object approached Earth undetected before its atmospheric entry, in part because its radiant (source direction) was close to the Sun. 1,491 people were injured seriously enough to seek medical treatment. All of the injuries were due to indirect effects rather than the meteor itself, mainly from broken glass from windows that were blown in when the shock wave arrived, minutes after the superbolide's flash. Around 7,200 buildings in six cities across the region were damaged [...] The light from the meteor was briefly brighter than the Sun [...] The blast created by the meteor's air burst produced extensive ground damage [...] The earlier-predicted and well-publicized close approach of a larger asteroid on the same day, the roughly 30 meters (100 feet) 367943 Duende, occurred about 16 hours later; the very different orbits of the two objects showed they were unrelated to each other. [...] The intense light from the meteor, momentarily brighter than the Sun, also produced injuries, resulting in more than 180 cases of eye pain [...] Twenty people reported ultraviolet burns similar to sunburn [...] A fourth-grade teacher in Chelyabinsk, Yulia Karbysheva, was hailed as a hero after saving 44 children from imploding window glass cuts. Despite not knowing the origin of the intense flash of light, Karbysheva thought it prudent to take precautionary measures by ordering her students to stay away from the room's windows and to perform a duck and cover manoeuvre and then to leave the building. Karbysheva, who remained standing, was seriously lacerated when the blast arrived and window glass severed a tendon in one of her arms and left thigh; none of her students, whom she ordered to hide under their desks, suffered cuts. [...] The United States space agency NASA estimated the diameter of the bolide at about 17 to 20 meters

gancho: O primeiro visitante confirmado de fora do Sistema Solar foi visto em 2017, já indo embora. Ele acelerou como um cometa que solta gás, mas não mostrou nenhuma nuvem de gás ou poeira. Do que era feito, ninguém sabe.
explicacao: ʻOumuamua foi descoberto em 19 de outubro de 2017 por um telescópio no Havaí, uns 40 dias depois de passar pelo ponto mais próximo do Sol. Já se afastava quando foi notado. A trajetória, fortemente hiperbólica, mostrou que ele não estava preso ao Sol: veio do espaço interestelar e para lá voltará. Por ser o primeiro do tipo, ganhou uma nova designação, "1I", de interestelar. O nome, em havaiano, quer dizer algo como "primeiro mensageiro distante". Primeiro foi chamado de cometa, depois de asteroide, porque imagens profundas não mostraram coma, a nuvem que envolve os cometas perto do Sol. Em 2018, porém, astrônomos mediram uma aceleração que a gravidade não explicava, compatível com um cometa soltando gás ou com a pressão da luz solar. As propostas se multiplicaram: gelo de nitrogênio, como um pedaço de um planeta parecido com Plutão; gelo de hidrogênio puro, depois considerado incapaz de sobreviver à viagem; e, em 2023, hidrogênio formado por radiação dentro de um corpo rico em gelo de água e liberado perto do Sol, o que faria dele um cometa interestelar parecido com os nossos. Em 2024 já se conheciam 14 asteroides com o mesmo comportamento estranho, hoje chamados de "cometas escuros". Mesmo assim, a composição dele continua desconhecida, e ele saiu de alcance dos telescópios em poucos meses.

fontes.trecho: 1I/ʻOumuamua is the first confirmed interstellar object detected passing through the Solar System. Formally designated 1I/2017 U1, it was discovered by Canadian physicist Robert Weryk using the Pan-STARRS telescope at Haleakalā Observatory, Hawaii, on 19 October 2017, approximately 40 days after it passed its closest point to the Sun on 9 September. [...] already heading away from the Sun. [...] Despite its close approach to the Sun, it showed no signs of having a coma,  the usual nebula around comets formed when they pass near the Sun. Further, it exhibited non‑gravitational acceleration, potentially due to outgassing or a push from solar radiation pressure. [...] It roughly translates to 'first distant messenger'. [...] A two-week observation arc had verified a strongly hyperbolic trajectory. [...] On 27 June 2018, astronomers reported a non-gravitational acceleration to ʻOumuamua's trajectory, potentially consistent with a push from solar radiation pressure. [...] However, it was later calculated that hydrogen icebergs cannot survive their journey through interstellar space. [...] Originally classified as comet C/2017 U1, it was later reclassified as asteroid A/2017 U1 due to the absence of a coma. Once it was unambiguously identified as coming from outside the Solar System, a new designation was created: I, for Interstellar object. [...] the compositional nature of the object continues to be unknown. [...] a piece of an exoplanet rich in nitrogen ice, similar to Pluto. [...] so it will eventually leave the Solar System and continue into interstellar space. [...] very deep stacked images were taken at the Very Large Telescope later the same day, but the object showed no presence of a coma. [...] in mid-December 2017, it was too faint and fast-moving to be studied by even the largest ground-based telescopes. [...] On 22 March 2023, astronomers proposed the observed acceleration was "due to the release of entrapped molecular hydrogen that formed through energetic processing of an H2O-rich icy body", consistent with ʻOumuamua being an interstellar comet [...] But by 2024, astronomers had identified 14 asteroids with the same unusual behavior. This makes ʻOumuamua the first member of another new class of objects called dark comets.

gancho: A poeira do asteroide Bennu, trazida à Terra em 2023, tem 14 dos 20 aminoácidos das proteínas e as cinco bases do DNA e do RNA. E tem um enigma: os aminoácidos vêm meio "canhotos", meio "destros", e os da vida não.
explicacao: A sonda OSIRIS-REx, da NASA, recolheu 121,6 gramas do asteroide Bennu e os entregou à Terra em 2023. As primeiras análises detalhadas, divulgadas em 2025, acharam 14 dos 20 aminoácidos que a vida terrestre usa para montar proteínas e todas as cinco bases nitrogenadas que guardam e transmitem instruções genéticas no DNA e no RNA. Havia também amônia em quantidade excepcional e formaldeído, que podem reagir e formar moléculas complexas como aminoácidos. Outro grupo identificou 11 minerais que se formam quando água com sais dissolvidos evapora devagar, como halita e calcita: sinal de uma antiga água salgada, um possível "caldo" para essas reações. Segundo a NASA, isso não é evidência de vida, mas sugere que as condições para ela surgir eram comuns no início do Sistema Solar. Fica a pergunta: muitos aminoácidos existem em duas versões espelhadas, como mão esquerda e mão direita. A vida na Terra usa quase só a esquerda, mas Bennu tem as duas na mesma proporção. Por que a vida "virou à esquerda" continua um mistério.

fontes.titulo: NASA's Asteroid Bennu Sample Reveals Mix of Life's Ingredients
fontes.trecho: a history of saltwater that could have served as the "broth" for these compounds to interact and combine. The findings do not show evidence for life itself, but they do suggest the conditions necessary for the emergence of life were widespread across the early solar system [...] the Bennu samples, which OSIRIS-REx delivered to Earth in 2023. [...] amino acids – 14 of the 20 that life on Earth uses to make proteins – and all five nucleobases that life on Earth uses to store and transmit genetic instructions in more complex terrestrial biomolecules, such as DNA and RNA [...] Scientists also described exceptionally high abundances of ammonia in the Bennu samples. Ammonia is important to biology because it can react with formaldehyde, which also was detected in the samples, to form complex molecules, such as amino acids [...] Ranging from calcite to halite and sylvite, scientists identified traces of 11 minerals in the Bennu sample that form as water containing dissolved salts evaporates over long periods of time [...] Many amino acids can be created in two mirror-image versions, like a pair of left and right hands. Life on Earth almost exclusively produces the left-handed variety, but the Bennu samples contain an equal mixture of both. [...] The reason life "turned left" instead of right remains a mystery.

In total, 121.6 g (4.29 oz) of asteroidal material was recovered from the sample container. [...] In January 2025, it was reported that a wide range of carbon- and nitrogen-rich organic compounds have been identified in samples returned from Bennu

gancho: Em 2020, a sonda OSIRIS-REx tocou o asteroide Bennu para colher amostras. A superfície era tão frouxa, de partículas mal presas umas às outras, que ela teria afundado se não acionasse logo os propulsores.
explicacao: Bennu tem uns 490 metros de diâmetro. Medições dos efeitos gravitacionais e térmicos deram uma densidade média só um pouco maior que a da água, o que sugere que uns 40% do interior sejam espaços vazios. Por isso, ele é visto como uma pilha de escombros: o material que o forma veio da quebra de um corpo muito maior. A sonda OSIRIS-REx, da NASA, tocou a superfície em 20 de outubro de 2020. No contato, um jato de gás nitrogênio soprou partículas menores que 2 cm para dentro do coletor, na ponta de um braço robótico. A análise posterior mostrou que as partículas da superfície estão frouxamente compactadas e pouco presas umas às outras. Segundo a NASA, a sonda teria afundado em Bennu se não tivesse disparado os propulsores para se afastar logo depois de pegar poeira e pedras. A coleta rendeu mais do que o necessário: pedras ficaram presas na aba que deveria manter a amostra no coletor, e parte do material passou a escapar devagar para o espaço, até o coletor ser guardado na cápsula de retorno.

fontes.trecho: 101955 Bennu has a mean diameter of 490 m [...] Analysis of the gravitational and thermal effects has given a bulk density of ρ = 1190±13 kg/m3, which is only slightly denser than water. Therefore, the predicted macroporosity is 40±10%, suggesting the interior has a rubble pile structure or even hollows. [...] Analysis showed that the particles making up Bennu's exterior are loosely packed and lightly bound to each other; "The spacecraft would have sunk into Bennu had it not fired its thrusters to back away immediately after it grabbed dust and rock from the asteroid's surface." [...] The carbonaceous material that composes Bennu came from the breakup of a much larger parent body

On 20 October 2020, OSIRIS-REx touched down on Bennu and successfully collected a sample. [...] Upon surface contact by the TAGSAM instrument, a burst of nitrogen gas was released to blow regolith particles smaller than 2 cm (0.8 in) into the sampler head at the end of the robotic arm. [...] NASA concluded that there were rocks wedged in the mylar flap meant to keep the sample inside, causing the sample to slowly escape into space. [...] more than the 60 g (2.1 oz) needed [...] With the collector head secure inside the SRC, pieces of the sample would no longer be lost.

fontes.titulo: Surprise Again: Asteroid Bennu Reveals Its Surface Is Like a Plastic Ball Pit
fontes.trecho: After analyzing data gathered when NASA's OSIRIS-REx spacecraft collected a sample from asteroid Bennu in October 2020, scientists have learned something astonishing: The spacecraft would have sunk into Bennu had it not fired its thrusters to back away immediately after it grabbed dust and rock from the asteroid's surface. It turns out that the particles making up Bennu's exterior are so loosely packed and lightly bound to each other

gancho: Após dez anos de viagem, o robô europeu Philae pousou num cometa em 2014, mas os arpões que deviam prendê-lo falharam. Ele quicou duas vezes e parou na sombra de um penhasco, onde só foi localizado em 2016.
explicacao: Philae viajou a bordo da sonda Rosetta, da Agência Espacial Europeia, e se soltou dela para descer no cometa 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko dez anos e oito meses depois de sair da Terra. Como a velocidade de escape do cometa é de cerca de 1 metro por segundo, ou menos, era preciso evitar que a sonda quicasse. Por isso, ela tinha arpões para se ancorar e um propulsor para segurá-la contra o chão. Em 12 de novembro de 2014, nenhum dos dois funcionou. Philae quicou duas vezes e parou inclinado, num terreno acidentado, aparentemente à sombra de um paredão. Mesmo assim, foi o primeiro pouso suave num núcleo de cometa, e a sonda enviou dados e as primeiras imagens da superfície de um cometa por cerca de 64 horas. A bateria principal fora feita para durar umas 60 horas, e no local o sol batia só 90 minutos a cada dia do cometa, de 12,4 horas, pouco para recarregar. Entre junho e julho de 2015, Philae voltou a se comunicar de vez em quando, mas o contato se perdeu de novo. Fotos da Rosetta de 2 de setembro de 2016 o acharam deitado de lado numa fenda funda, à sombra de um penhasco. Semanas depois, a Rosetta encerrou a missão se chocando contra o mesmo cometa.

fontes.trecho: a robotic European Space Agency lander that accompanied the Rosetta spacecraft until it separated to land on comet 67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko, ten years and eight months after departing Earth. On 12 November 2014, Philae touched down on the comet, but it bounced when its anchoring harpoons failed to deploy and a thruster designed to hold the probe to the surface did not fire. After bouncing off the surface twice, Philae achieved the first-ever "soft" (nondestructive) landing on a comet nucleus, although the lander's final, uncontrolled touchdown left it in a non-optimal location and orientation. Philae transmitted images and data back to earth for about 64 hours. Despite the landing problems, the probe's instruments obtained the first images from a comet's surface. [...] to avoid bouncing as the comet's escape velocity is only around 1 m/s [...] It sits in rough terrain, apparently in the shadow of a nearby cliff or crater wall, and is canted at an angle of around 30 degrees [...] The primary battery was designed to power the instruments for about 60 hours. [...] but the limited sunlight (90 minutes per 12.4-hour comet day) at the actual landing site was inadequate to maintain Philae's activities [...] Philae communicated sporadically with Rosetta from 13 June to 9 July 2015, but contact was then lost. [...] Its location was finally identified in photographs taken by Rosetta on 2 September 2016 as the orbiter was sent on orbits closer to the comet. The now-silent Philae was lying on its side in a deep crack in the shadow of a cliff. [...] On 30 September 2016, the Rosetta spacecraft ended its mission by crashing in the comet's Ma'at region.

gancho: Em 1954, um meteorito furou o telhado de uma casa no Alabama e atingiu Ann Hodges no sofá. Depois, disputou a pedra com a dona da casa alugada e não lucrou nada. Quem lucrou foi um agricultor que achou outro pedaço.
explicacao: Ann Hodges cochilava em casa, em Sylacauga, quando um fragmento de 3,86 kg atravessou o telhado, quicou num rádio e a acertou na coxa e na mão. Ficou só com um grande hematoma, e é tida como a primeira pessoa documentada a ser atingida por um meteorito e sobreviver. A pedra foi confiscada pela polícia e entregue à Força Aérea dos EUA. Enquanto a pedra estava na base aérea, segundo o marido de Ann, chegaram várias ofertas, uma delas de quase 5.500 dólares, que não podiam ser aceitas. A pedra também virou disputa: a proprietária do imóvel alugado a reivindicou, por ter caído na sua propriedade. O casal Hodges fechou acordo e pagou 500 dólares a ela. Quando o meteorito voltou às mãos deles, mais de um ano depois, o interesse do público tinha passado e não apareceu comprador. Em 1956, a pedra foi parar no museu de história natural do Alabama: os registros falam em doação, e o marido lembrava de uma venda, contra a vontade dele, por uns 25 dólares. Já um agricultor da região, Julius McKinney, achou no dia seguinte à queda o segundo maior fragmento, comprado por um advogado para o Smithsonian. Com o dinheiro, a família dele comprou um carro e uma casa.

fontes.trecho: The Sylacauga meteorite fell on November 30, 1954 [...] It split into at least three fragments, with one of the fragments falling through a roof and then landing on Hodges, who was napping on her couch. [...] The meteorite left a 3-foot (91 cm) wide hole in the roof of her house, bounced off a console radio, and hit her on her upper thigh and hand, giving her a large bruise. [...] The meteorite was confiscated by the Sylacauga police chief, who then turned it over to the United States Air Force. [...] Both the Hodgeses and their landlord, Bertie Guy, claimed ownership of the rock, Guy's claim being that it had fallen on her property. The Hodgeses and Guy settled, with the Hodgeses paying $500 for the rock. However, by the time it was returned to the Hodgeses, over a year later, public attention had diminished, and they were unable to then find a buyer. The day after the fall, local farmer Julius McKinney came upon the second-largest fragment from the same meteorite. An Indianapolis-based lawyer bought it for the Smithsonian Institution. The McKinney family was able to use the money to buy a car and a house. [...] The Hodges fragment (3.86 kilograms (8.5 lb)) [...] was an American woman known for being the first documented individual to be struck by a meteorite and survive.
